title: Community Relations & Visitor Experience Manager
description:
Language requirements: English essential
Level: PM-05
Who can apply: Nunavut Inuit who are enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement.
About the position
Duties
The CRVE Manager will work closely with the parks' joint management committees and the
surrounding communities, providing visitor services to the National Park. This position will require you
to perform the following duties:
• Oversee visitor and community operations in the context of the Nunavut Agreement and the
Inuit Impact and Benefit Agreements for the parks.
• Participate as an active member of the Nunavut Field Unit management team.
• Manage financial and human resources, including supervising a team.
• Meet with park management committees and Inuit Knowledge working groups to share
information and seek advice.
• Plan and deliver visitor experience opportunities, and administer business licensing/permitting
programs.
• Oversee the development and delivery of community events, training opportunities, workshops,
and school programs.
• Develop partnerships and/or work with stakeholders.
Training, Development & Education Opportunities: Multi-year career development plans which include
opportunities for education assistance funding and training opportunities are available.
Work environment
Parks Canada Agency is a federal government agency responsible for the protection and presentation of Canada’s natural and cultural resources through a system of national parks, national marine conservation areas and national historic sites in all regions of Canada.
In Nunavut, Inuit and Parks Canada cooperatively manage five national parks, one national historic site and one national marine conservation area. They are: Auyuittuq National Park, Sirmilik National Park, Qausuittuq National Park, Quttinirpaaq National Park, Ukkusiksalik National Park, the Wrecks of HMS Erebus and HMS Terror National Historic Site and Tallurutiup Imanga National Marine Conservation Area. Long before these areas received federal protection, Inuit lived, harvested and travelled these lands and waters. Many staff have connections to these places through their families and ancestors. To this day, harvesting and use by Inuit remains a protected right under the Nunavut Agreement. As a Parks Canada team member in Nunavut, you will help protect, present and share these incredible places so they remain for generations, by implementing the Nunavut Agreement and Inuit Impact and Benefit Agreements.
Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values. Diverse teams bring different perspectives and creative ideas that benefit our clients, the communities we serve and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from individuals with diverse abilities and from all backgrounds and identities.
Intent of the process
To staff a 1.0 full-time, indeterminate PM-05 CRVE Manager position in Resolute, NU (Quttinirpaaq and
Qausuittuq) & 1.0 full-time, term PM-05 CRVE Manager position in Pangnirtung, NU (Auyuittuq)
This process may be used to create a list of qualified candidates to staff similar positions with various
tenures including: indeterminate, acting, assignment, and specified period , full-time or part-time, with
various security levels or linguistic requirements in same or other parts of Nunavut and Canada.

The Explosives Regulatory Division administers and enforces the Explosives Act and the Explosives Regulations, 2013, to ensure the safe and secure manufacture, storage, acquisition, transport and sale of explosives in Canada. title: Senior Analytical Technologist
description:
Language requirements: English essential
Level: EG-05
Who can apply: Persons residing in Canada, and Canadian citizens and Permanent residents abroad.
About the position
Duties
The EG-05 position is responsible for performing and supporting advanced analytical laboratory activities within the Analytical Chemistry Laboratory (ACL) at Natural Resources Canada. The incumbent independently conducts chemical analyses of environmental, geological, and other complex samples using various analytical techniques and instrumentation, including ICP-MS, ICP-AES, ion chromatography (IC), total organic carbon (TOC), and elemental analysis systems.
The position involves sample preparation, including digestion and other sample treatment procedures, instrument operation, calibration, maintenance, troubleshooting, and verification of analytical results. The incumbent is also responsible for implementing and following laboratory quality assurance and quality control procedures, contributing to the development and revision of standard operating procedures, maintaining accurate laboratory records, and preparing technical reports.
In addition, the position requires collaboration with laboratory colleagues, chemists, and NRCan scientists to support analytical requirements, improve laboratory methods, and contribute to research projects related to critical minerals, environmental analysis, and other departmental priorities. The incumbent must work safely, manage competing priorities, and ensure that analytical work is completed accurately, efficiently, and within established deadlines.
Intent of the process
The intent of this process is to staff one term position in Ottawa, ON until March 31, 2028.
A pool of (fully or partially qualified) candidates will be established through this process to staff identical or similar positions within Natural Resources Canada with various tenures, language requirements/ profile(s), security requirements, conditions of employment and for various locations.

title: Bilingual Senior Specialist, Client Relations
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
About the role
Join the Insurance Business Development team, in the Senior Specialist, Client Relations position. In this role, you will draw on your extensive knowledge of homeowner mortgage loan insurance (HO MLI) policy and lender operations to provide strategic thought leadership, advice and enablement to the National Key Account Manager and regional teams. You will support the development, communication and cascade of lender strategic plans into coordinated regional activities, serving as a key liaison with internal partners to align priorities, resolve operational issues and strengthen the client experience.
This is a temporary position with a duration of 18 months.
What you'll do:
- Support the National Key Account Manager in developing and monitoring lender strategic plans aligned with corporate priorities, client needs and market intelligence, and coordinate their cascade into regional engagement plans, activities and key performance indicators.
- Provide strategic thought leadership by synthesizing lender insights, business performance, client feedback and competitive trends into actionable recommendations that inform account priorities, business development opportunities and the client experience.
- Provide guidance on HO MLI policies, products and operational requirements, working with internal subject-matter experts to support consistent interpretation, address complex inquiries and identify process or program improvements.
- Liaise with lender head office and operational contacts to understand mortgage origination and insurance workflows, identify recurring needs and coordinate solutions that support consistent national practices and effective service delivery.
- Coordinate planning, business reviews and follow-up with the National Key Account Manager and regional teams, clarifying actions, responsibilities and timelines, monitoring progress and escalating risks or barriers to implementation.
- Serve as a liaison with internal policy, underwriting, operations and other business partners to align lender initiatives, resolve complex or sensitive issues and communicate client needs and emerging risks.
- Develop coordinated communications, briefing materials, tools and training that equip the National Key Account Manager and regional teams to communicate lender priorities, implement initiatives and share knowledge consistently.
- Provide coaching and advisory support to national and regional teams, sharing HO MLI expertise and best practices and bringing regional feedback into national planning to strengthen execution and continuous improvement.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in a field relevant to real estate (e.g., business administration, finance, economics, or commerce), or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
- A minimum of seven (7) years of relevant experience in client relationships and operations.
- Comprehensive knowledge of HO MLI policies, products and operational requirements, and strong understanding of lender mortgage origination, underwriting and insurance processes.
- Strong strategic thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to synthesize client insights, market intelligence, and performance data into practical advice and recommendations.
- Superior written and verbal communication skills in both official languages (English and French), including the ability to influence and negotiate; able to deliver clear, persuasive presentations and gain acceptance of proposals or plans.
- The ability to build effective relationships with lender contacts and internal partners, facilitate cross-functional collaboration, and provide coaching and advisory support to national and regional teams.
- Superior problem-solving skills and sound judgment in resolving complex policy and operational issues and identifying risks requiring escalation.
- Strong planning and coordination skills, with the ability to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans and manage concurrent initiatives in ambiguous, fast-paced environments.
It would be great if you also had:
- An MBA, PMP, Lean Six Sigma designation, or experience in residential mortgage lending, national account planning or operational improvement initiatives.
- Extensive working knowledge and experience with CRM and Dynamics 365.

You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.

We are looking for a Manager of Workplace Programs to support our Human Resources Branch. The Manager of Workplace Programs would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity. You will lead a work unit responsible for leading NRC programs and initiatives in the areas of Harassment and Violence Prevention and Resolution (HVPR), Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI), wellness, and Official Languages (OL).
In this role, you will oversee the HVPR intake, case management and resolution processes and provide leadership for program and process improvements that strengthen prevention, resolution and support mechanisms. You will also lead and oversee the advancement of the NRC’s EDI strategy and programs and policies that foster a respectful, inclusive, healthy and bilingual workplace.

Join the Infrastructure and Operations team, in the Bilingual Senior Specialist, IT Operations Monitoring & Service Insights position. The primary focus of this role is the hands-on monitoring of infrastructure, applications, and end-to-end services to provide reliable operational visibility and enable proactive incident detection. You will help evaluate and select enterprise monitoring and observability tools, configure new platforms and monitoring capabilities from the ground up, maintain and continuously improve them, and define the event and alert management processes and procedures that support effective operational response.
What you’ll do:
- Own and continuously improve monitoring coverage for infrastructure, networks, cloud platforms, applications, certificates, integrations, and critical end-to-end services.
- Evaluate business and technical requirements and help select fit-for-purpose monitoring, observability, logging, and security analytics tools such as Zabbix, Dynatrace, SolarWinds, PRTG, Azure Monitor, Azure Log Analytics, Splunk, and Microsoft Sentinel.
- Configure and implement monitoring platforms and capabilities from the ground up, including discovery, agents, collectors, integrations, dashboards, service maps, health checks, log ingestion, alerts, and automated ticket creation.
- Maintain, administer, upgrade, and optimize monitoring tools and integrations to ensure reliable data collection, platform availability, appropriate capacity, security, and sustainable support.
- Define, document, and govern event and alert management processes and procedures, including standards for thresholds, severity, correlation, deduplication, suppression, escalation, ownership, and response.
- Detect, validate, enrich, correlate, and route events and alerts to identify service degradation and incidents before users are affected, reduce alert noise, and accelerate triage.
- Use monitoring data, logs, service-level indicators, and operational trends to identify detection gaps and improve service reliability, operational readiness, mean time to detect (MTTD), and mean time to restore or resolve (MTTR).
- Partner with application, infrastructure, security, service management, and vendor teams to establish monitoring requirements, onboard services, support incidents and post-incident reviews, and provide actionable operational insights.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in Information Systems, Business, or a related field, and a minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in IT operations, including substantial hands-on responsibility for enterprise monitoring, observability, service reliability, or Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) (an equivalent combination of related education and/or experience will be considered).
- A demonstrated experience designing, configuring, and implementing monitoring or observability platforms from the ground up and supporting them through their operational lifecycle.
- A strong knowledge of infrastructure, application, cloud, network, service, log, synthetic, and availability monitoring, including practical experience defining dashboards, health indicators, alerts, and service-level measurements.
- Experience defining and operating event and alert management practices, including threshold design, alert tuning, correlation, deduplication, noise reduction, escalation, and on-call integration.
- The ability to assess monitoring requirements, compare tools, develop selection criteria, conduct proofs of concept, and recommend solutions based on coverage, integration, scalability, usability, security, and total cost of ownership.
- A working knowledge of ITIL and ITSM processes, particularly Incident, Major Incident, Problem, Change, Configuration, and Event Management; an ITIL Foundation certification is required.
- A record of using monitoring and operational data to improve MTTD, reduce MTTR, strengthen operational readiness, and increase service reliability in complex enterprise environments.
- Strong analytical, documentation, facilitation, and communication skills in both official languages (English and French), with the ability to work calmly across technical and business teams during high-pressure situations.
Technologies:
- A hands-on experience with several enterprise monitoring and observability platforms, such as Zabbix, Dynatrace, SolarWinds, PRTG, Azure Monitor, Azure Log Analytics, Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, or comparable tools.
- Experience integrating monitoring platforms with ServiceNow ITSM or comparable service management tools for event ingestion, alert enrichment, incident creation, routing, dashboards, and reporting.
- A familiarity with logs, metrics, traces, APIs, agents, collectors, scripting or automation, cloud and hybrid environments, and technologies that support end-to-end service visibility.
It will be great if you also had:
- Experience with observability engineering, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), service-level objectives, error budgets, or reliability practices in cloud and hybrid environments.
- Experience automating monitoring configuration, alert enrichment, remediation, or operational workflows using APIs, scripts, infrastructure as code, or orchestration tools.
- Experience coordinating vendors and managed service providers, leading monitoring onboarding or modernization initiatives, or developing operational readiness standards for new and changed services.
- Advanced ITIL, monitoring, observability, cloud, security, Splunk, Dynatrace, Microsoft, or SRE-related certifications.

title: Student, Communications and Digital Content
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Staffing process 26-PB-18
Position Student, part-time
Pay $18.69 to $38.38 per hour, based on academic level (college, undergraduate, master's or doctoral), in accordance with the Treasury Board student rates of pay
Open to Canadian citizens, permanent residents and holders of a valid work permit who are legally able to work in Canada
Location Ottawa, hybrid
Schedule 15 to 30 hours per week, with flexibility to accommodate academic commitments and operational needs
Term January, 2027 to January, 2028, with the possibility of extension
Language Bilingual imperative (CBC)

We're looking for a creative, bilingual student with excellent writing skills who can help make complex economic and fiscal information clear, accessible and engaging for Parliamentarians, journalists and Canadians.
From news releases and digital storytelling to videos, animation and social media, this is an opportunity to contribute fresh ideas while gaining valuable experience in a unique parliamentary environment.
The Parliamentary Budget Office (PBO) provides independent economic and financial analysis to the Senate and House of Commons, analyzes the estimates of the government and, if requested, estimates the financial cost of any proposal over which Parliament has jurisdiction. The PBO is committed to serving Parliament with integrity and professionalism by providing independent, credible and non-partisan economic and financial analysis on a timely basis.
What you'll do
Working under the direction of the Director of Corporate Services, you will provide support in the following areas:
- Writing and editing: Draft news releases, website content, backgrounders and other communications materials in English and French. Final versions follow the PBO's translation and revision process.
- Editorial support: Support the plain-language review of reports for clarity, readability and consistency, in collaboration with analysts and the communications team.
- Creative digital content: Develop ideas for social media posts, short videos, animations, infographics and other digital media assets.
- Media and social media monitoring: Review news coverage, commentary and social media discussions relating to the PBO. Identify emerging issues, relevant trends and possible opportunities for engagement for staff review.
- Communications support: Support staff with report releases, the preparation of responses to media inquiries, key messages and other communications activities.
Essential qualifications
- Full-time enrolment in a college, undergraduate or graduate program in journalism, communications, digital media or a related field.
- Bilingual imperative, assessed through House of Commons language testing: Reading comprehension: Superior level (C) Written expression: Intermediate level (B) Oral interaction: Superior level (C)
- Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.
- Creativity, sound judgment and strong attention to detail.
- Familiarity with social media platforms and digital content creation.
- Ability to work collaboratively, manage priorities and respect the PBO's independent, non-partisan mandate.
Asset qualifications
- Experience with video production, animation, graphic design or multimedia storytelling.
Why join the PBO?
You'll work alongside experienced analysts on issues that matter to Canadians, including housing, health care, government spending and the economy. If you have an interest in public affairs, journalism, economics or government, you'll build your editorial and digital communications skills while helping make important research more accessible.
We know that great ideas come from everywhere. The PBO is committed to building a team with varied lived experiences, perspectives, ways of thinking and cultural backgrounds. We welcome applications from students with diverse experiences and creative approaches.
Conditions of employment
- Obtain and maintain reliability status.
- Maintain the confidentiality of embargoed reports and other information obtained in the course of employment.
- Maintain political neutrality consistent with the PBO's non-partisan mandate.
- Remain enrolled in full-time studies for the duration of the appointment.
- Satisfactory references and proof of enrolment.
How to apply
Apply through the PBO careers portal. Create a profile and follow the online instructions to submit your résumé, proof of full-time enrolment (unofficial copies are accepted at this stage) and two samples of your writing or creative digital work by the closing date. You may apply in English or French. For questions about this opportunity, contact pbohr@parl.gc.ca .
If you are currently employed in the federal public service or by a parliamentary entity, please identify your employment status (indeterminate, determinate, student or casual), substantive group and level, and current second language evaluation results in your application.
Accommodation: The PBO is committed to an accessible, barrier-free selection process. If you require accommodation at any stage, please contact pbohr@parl.gc.ca . Information you provide will be treated confidentially.
Privacy: Personal information you provide will be used only for this selection process.
Only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. We thank all those who apply.

About the position
Duties
About the position
Are you curious, analytical and motivated by work that makes a difference? Are you a self-starter who thrives in a work environment when you are responsible for advancing the organization’s priorities? As an Investigator at the Office of the Information Commissioner of Canada (OIC), you will help protect Canadians’ right to access information held by federal institutions. This role is an opportunity to use your critical thinking, problem-solving, research and communication skills to address challenging questions, uncover facts and contribute to fair and impartial outcomes.
What You'll Do:
•Investigate complaints made under the Access to Information Act
•Examine evidence
•Interpret and apply legislation
•Engage with individuals and organizations
•Develop well-supported findings on complex issues.
At the OIC, your work will have a meaningful impact on transparency, accountability and public trust. You will join a team of dedicated professionals who value integrity, collaboration, sound judgment and excellence. We welcome candidates who have developed relevant skills and experience in a variety of fields, including investigations, regulatory compliance, auditing, dispute resolution, research or other roles requiring objective analysis and evidence-based decision-making.
If you enjoy examining complex issues, working with the public, weighing different perspectives and producing clear, defensible conclusions, we invite you to bring your skills and experience to work that serves the public interest. Our office is located at 30 Victoria Street in Gatineau, Quebec.
A Career with Opportunities to Grow
At the Office of the Information Commissioner, we invest in the professional growth and development of our investigators. Through our structured Professional Development Program, successful participants have the opportunity to progress from a PM-03 to the PM-06 level, building their investigative expertise, analytical skills and professional capabilities along the way.
It's an opportunity to build a rewarding career while making a meaningful contribution to transparency and accountability in the federal government.
Intent of the process
The immediate need is to staff ten (10) positions. A pool of partially qualified candidates may be established to staff similar positions with various tenures, various linguistic profiles as well as various security clearances within the Office of the Information Commissioner of Canada.
Upon request, if a pool is established through this selection process, it may be shared with other federal organizations listed in Schedules I, IV and V of the Financial Administration Act (FAA) to staff similar positions within their organizations.
Positions to be filled
10
Important messages
The Office of the Information Commissioner of Canada (OIC) is an inclusive and diverse organization that offers its employees the opportunity to perform challenging duties aimed at protecting Canadians’ quasi-constitutional right to access to information.
The Information Commissioner of Canada, as an independent Agent of Parliament, is responsible for ensuring compliance with the right of access set out in Part 1 of the Access to Information Act. She investigates complaints regarding access to information requests made to federal institutions subject to the Act. She advises Parliament and its committees on matters relating to the state of the access to information system, promotes changes that could reform the Act, and fosters its implementation.
The effectiveness of this mandate depends on the trust of Parliament, federal institutions, complainants, and the public. To preserve this trust, the Commissioner must maintain her independence, objectivity, and impartiality at all times, both in the investigative activities conducted by the Office of the Information Commissioner and in the exercise of her role as an Agent of Parliament and the other functions and powers conferred by the Act.
To this end, any personal, professional, or other situation involving a candidate that could give rise to an actual, apparent, or potential conflict of interest relating to the Commissioner’s mandate must be proactively identified, prevented, or resolved.
A variety of assessment methods can be used, such as interviews, written examinations, achievement records, performance appraisals and references.
Each person has the right to participate in an appointment process in the official language(s) of their choice.
Management may choose to invoke an asset(s) at any point of the process.
When submitting your application to this selection process, you will be prompted to answer screening questions concerning the education and experiences requirements listed in the essential qualifications and asset qualifications section. It is your responsibility to provide clear and concrete examples in your responses to each question. It is recommended that you describe the experience examples in specific terms, providing sufficient details so that the Assessment Board can clearly understand. Describe the situation/task, how, when and where you acquired these experiences by giving examples. Content of your response must be supported by your CV/resume as your responses to these questions will be used as a primary source of information and your CV/resume will only be used to validate this information. Should you indicate in your response "please refer to CV/resume" your application will be rejected. Lack of examples and details will result in your application being rejected as the Assessment Board will have insufficient information to determine if the requirement is met.

Because of this operational requirement, applicants may be asked, during the selection process, to provide any relevant information that would identify any personal, professional, or other circumstances that could give rise to an actual, apparent, or potential conflict of interest relating to the Commissioner’s mandate. These situations could arise, in particular, from current or prior employment or from current, prior, or anticipated involvement in a complaint, proceeding, or litigation related to the Access to Information Act or to any other duties or powers exercised by the Commissioner under that Act.

About the position
Duties
As part of the Supreme Court of Canada Library team, the Senior Librarian, Digital Library Services will:
• Lead technology projects to develop, improve and modernize library systems, tools and services, with a focus on supporting legal research and improving business processes.
• Evaluate, implement and maintain digital tools and applications to ensure they meet users' needs and support the Court's operations.
• Explore emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and collaboration tools, and recommend opportunities to improve legal research, information sharing and library services.

Work environment
The Supreme Court of Canada (SCC) is Canada’s final court of appeal. The SCC is a bilingual institution that hears cases in French and English, in all areas of the law, such as family, criminal, and constitutional law. It decides cases from Canada’s two major legal traditions, common and civil law. Its decisions affect the lives of all Canadians. The SCC recognizes that a key element necessary in achieving and retaining a representative workforce is providing a supportive work environment and fostering a corporate culture that is welcoming to all employees, including designated group members. According to the most recent public service employee surveys, the SCC is one of the best places to work in the federal public service. Given that the SCC is not served by Pay Center, it has its own compensation team responsible for administering the full range of pay and benefit transactions in Phoenix and MyGCHR.

title: Director, Co-Innovation Programs (#26366)
description:

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are looking for an experienced and dynamic Director, Co-Innovation Programs for the Industrial Research Assistance Program. The Director would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
Working with clients and partners, the National Research Council Canada provides strategic research, innovation support, scientific and technical services to develop and deploy solutions to meet Canada’s current and future industrial and societal needs.
The NRC Industrial Research Assistance Program (NRC IRAP) is a critical component of the NRC with a clear mandate to support SMEs’ growth through innovation. The NRC IRAP has professional field staff that work with clients and give strategic advice to assist the firms with their overall development. The NRC IRAP also can provide financial support to these SMEs’ innovation projects.
As Director, Co-Innovation working closely with your Director General, other Director(s) Co-Innovation and with senior managers and executives across the organization, you will use your own STI network domestically and internationally, understanding and relationships to design and execute strategies and agreements that are important to NRC and to Canada. As a natural leader, you will energize and build a strong team to serve the corporation and you will negotiate with diverse groups within NRC and around the globe to bring ideas and strategies to life. Committed to excellence, you will use your initiative to make recommendations for continuous improvement project management practices and tools.

A university degree, preferably in engineering, sciences, public or business administration, international relations, or other relevant fields.
Preference may be given to those with graduate studies in relevant fields.

- Extensive and recent experience at the Executive level in providing strategic advice and counsel to ministerial staff and senior level executives including Presidents, Vice Presidents and/or other equivalent positions in the public or private sectors, on complex initiatives.
- Extensive business experience in developing domestic and/or international partnerships and managing client relationships with private sector firms and government department.
- Experience in designing international strategies, developing opportunities and negotiating bi-lateral agreements within an innovation context.
- Significant recent experience in leading and managing human and financial resources;
- Significant experience in designing domestic and/or international strategies, developing opportunities and negotiating agreements within an innovation context.

The Communications Security Establishment (CSE) is Canada’s agency responsible for foreign signals intelligence, cyber operations and cyber security. Learn more about our mission , and what it means to work in a security and intelligence field .
CSE is committed to fostering a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion. This isn’t just an ideal, it’s crucial to our mission. Find out about our workplace culture , including our diversity and inclusion initiatives.
Become part of our team and you’ll understand why CSE is the most important organization you’ve never heard of (YouTube) .
Job summary
Join the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security , a part of CSE, and contribute to projects that help strengthen Canada's cyber security posture and support the safety and security of Canadians.
You will work as part of a collaborative development team responsible for the administration, development, and enhancement of a Microsoft (MS) Dynamics 365 and Dataverse platform. As a MS Dynamics 365 developer you will design and implement innovative solutions, develop integrations with enterprise systems, automate business processes, and help deliver reliable services that support the mission of the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.
Whether you are an entry-level, intermediate, or experienced developer, you will have the opportunity to work on meaningful projects, expand your technical expertise, and contribute to a culture of continuous learning, innovation, and knowledge-sharing.

- Development duties: develop Microsoft (MS) Dynamics 365 and solution maintenance and configuration develop and maintain custom plugins and automations for Microsoft Dynamics 365 develop integrations and custom components for Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Dataverse, including data lake synchronization jobs, AI-enabled Model Context Protocol servers and tools and API integrations develop data migration tools for migrating customer data into MS Dynamics 365 build MS Dynamics 365 dashboards, workflows and reports perform code reviews and ensure adherence to development standards

Work environment
We believe that our employees are the cornerstone of achieving our goals. This is why we offer them a positive and inclusive work environment that is worthy of their dedication and professionalism. We promote career advancement by providing opportunities to develop and acquire new skills and competencies. We value diversity as well as the use of both official languages.
DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION
CSC remains committed to developing and maintaining a strong, inclusive, and diverse workforce that not only reflects the Canadian population, but also the populations we serve. We don’t just accept diversity – we celebrate it! We are making targeted efforts to recruit and retain diverse employees. In fact, CSC is the largest employer of Indigenous peoples in the core public administration. We believe that our ability to deliver accessible and inclusive services is realized when we recognize and retain the most diverse range of thoughts, experiences, and skills. We work hard to create an environment where all perspectives and experiences are valued. We are committed to helping diverse talent thrive.
We encourage women, Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, and members of visible minority groups to apply and to self-declare themselves as part of one or more of the Employment Equity groups as selection may be limited to candidates belonging to one or more of these groups.
CSC is seeking interest from persons looking for an exciting and rewarding career as a Parole Officer.
MAKE A DIFFERENCE!
Parole Officers are essential to fulfilling the Correctional Service of Canada's (CSC) mission of enhancing public safety by actively encouraging and assisting offenders to become law-abiding citizens, while exercising reasonable, safe, secure, and humane control. They play an active role to help offenders reintegrate into society.
With more than 20,000 employees, CSC plays a key role in contributing to public safety, working around the clock at our 43 correctional institutions, 91 parole offices and 14 community correctional centres across Canada. Join us to help change lives and protect Canadians!
The Parole Officer’s responsibilities include guiding the progress of offenders through a progression from most restrictive to least restrictive controls and from institutions to community supervision. They ensure that legal and policy requirements for reintegration are met as well as manage the reintegration of offenders throughout their sentences while trying to maintain public safety. Furthermore, they are responsible for assessing, analyzing and recommending potential transfer and release suitability of offenders as well as observing and interpreting the behaviour of the offenders/parolees. For more information on the responsibilities of a Parole Officer, please visit the following website: https://www.csc-scc.gc.ca/careers/003001-1103-eng.shtml

About the position
Duties
Correctional Program Officers (CPOs) and Indigenous Correctional Program Officers (ICPOs) deliver correctional programs that help offenders address the factors contributing to their criminal behaviour and develop the skills needed for safe reintegration into the community. They motivate participants, reinforce prosocial behaviour, and support offenders in meeting the objectives of their correctional or Healing Plans.
As members of the Case Management Team, CPOs/ICPOs assess program needs, evaluate progress, prepare reports, and share relevant information to support case management and decision-making. They facilitate group and individual sessions, review offender assignments, and ensure program delivery aligns with national standards and quality requirements.
ICPOs deliver Indigenous correctional programs grounded in Indigenous worldviews, teachings, cultural practices, and ceremony. They work closely with Elders and Spiritual Advisors, integrate cultural knowledge into interventions, and consider Indigenous Social History when assessing needs and progress. ICPOs may also deliver mainstream correctional programs when required.
Both roles collaborate with Parole Officers, Psychologists, Elders, Security, and other CSC staff to ensure coordinated interventions that support risk reduction and public safety. They manage group dynamics, respond to challenging behaviours, and contribute to a supportive learning environment.

The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) is the federal government agency responsible for administering sentences of a term of two years or more, as imposed by the courts. title: Team Leader, Deployed Operations
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Occasional travel to remote overseas theatres (ex. Latvia, Kuwait, Jamaica, etc.) will be required for this position to support Canadian Forces deployed situations.
Access to the sites is either by CAF service flight or commercial flight.
The Team Leader, Deployed Operations, leads and manages DCC’s deployed operations program. The incumbent supervises the delivery of DCC services to support of overseas infrastructure projects for the Client-Partners, in particular the Canadian Joint Operations Command (CJOC), Canadian Forces Joint Operational Support Group (CFJOSG), 1 Engineer Support Unit (1 ESU) and the Task Force Engineering Team in each overseas location. The incumbent identifies opportunities for deployment, the minimum job requirements and the necessary training, leads the development and management of all service level arrangements for overseas deployments, and works with DCC’s regions to create and maintain records related to employees scheduled to be deployed. When required, the incumbent deploys on short notice to fill capacity gaps (one to six weeks) and for meetings, quality assurance activities and site visits.
KEY AND PERIODIC ACTIVITIES The duties and responsibilities listed below are representative but not all-inclusive: Primary
- Manage, track and report on all overseas programs, including those for CJOC, CFJOSG and 1 ESU
- Manage and review list of deployed employees and track all pre-deployment activities
- Participate in procurement planning and assist with statement of work reviews and discussions related to deployed operations
- Review threat and risk levels for deployment locations
- Coordinate DCC, DND and CAF training and related requirements for all deployed staff
- Coordinate pre- and post-deployment medical screenings, insurance, assignment letters and related documents with Human Resources
- Coordinate with DND Honours and Recognition to have DCC deployed staff recognized for their support overseas
- Prepare briefings and weekly reports for the Senior Management Group
- Support Client-Partners’ industrial security requirements for overseas locations
- Coordinate and lead all weekly update teleconferences with deployed staff
- Offer support outside of standard business hours to coordinate urgent matters with deployed staff
- Collaborate with deployed individuals’ team leader and site manager (from their substantive position) to carry out all business management tasks (e.g. time entry, expense claims, determining start and end dates for temporary assignments, performance evaluations)
- Perform human resources functions for deployed staff (e.g. coach, supervise, mentor, plan and allocate resources, and manage performance)

- DCC service lines
- Business management
- Project management, contracting and contract management

We’ve got the purpose, the people and the perks you need for a fulfilling career. Here’s the comprehensive and generous benefits you get when you’re a permanent employee:

- Comprehensive group insurance plan to support your well-being from day one.
- Support towards your personal and professional growth with training, mentorship and more.

About the role
Join the People and Culture team, in the Bilingual Specialist, Employee Relations position. In this role, you will provide expert advice, coaching and guidance to employees, people leaders and HR Business Partners to resolve human relations and work-related situations. You will plan, develop, implement and advise on Employee Relations policies, programs and services, as well as ensure compliance with CMHC's Code of Ethics and Business Conduct and Conflict of Interest Policy. You will also promote and ensure fair and equitable treatment of all employees and a productive work environment, consistent with CMHC values.
What you will do:
- Ensure compliance with legislative requirements on all existing and new Human Resources and Employee Relations policies and programs.
- Research, advise, analyze and coach people leaders, HR colleagues and employees regarding resolution of complaints and/or grievances and the implementation of appropriate corrective action, acting as a facilitator or mediator in discussions designed to address interpersonal or work-related conflicts.
- Act as subject matter expert and point of escalation on complex human resources management and employee relations issues.
- Develop and deliver communications, training and educational materials and sessions to ensure all staff and people leaders are aware of appropriate employee relations issues, programs, policies and services.
- Conduct fact findings and/or investigations into events surrounding workplace issues or complaints, as well as prepare reports of findings and recommend remedial actions.
- Receive and process notices of occurrences of workplace harassment and violence or other misconduct.
- Research, analyze and prepare comprehensive analyses, briefings and/or responses to complaints filed with the Canadian Human Rights Commission, unions (i.e., grievances).
- Support the collective bargaining process and negotiations, including the implementation of new collective agreements.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree, preferably in human resources management, business administration, industrial relations or other related fields.
- A minimum of five (5) years’ experience and understanding in human resources management and employee relations policies, practices, theories, concepts and systems. An equivalent of education and experience will be considered.
- Extensive knowledge and understanding of human resources management and employee relations policies, practices, theories, concepts, and systems.
- A working knowledge and understanding of federal employment law and regulations, relevant legislative issues, industry trends and practices.
- Experience in facilitation, mediation and conflict resolution with excellent consulting and interpersonal skills (strong negotiation, influencing and coaching skills).
- Demonstrated advanced written and oral communication skills in both official languages (French and English).
- A demonstrated ability to work in an automated environment, with particular emphasis on MS Suite and case management systems.

description:

Join the Business Solutions Engineering team, in the Senior Specialist, Software Engineering (Microsoft Dynamics 365 & Azure) position. In this role, you will be responsible for the design and implementation of secure, scalable, and maintainable end-to-end solutions. You will work closely with business and technical stakeholders to translate requirements into technical solutions while providing technical leadership, mentoring other developers, and supporting continuous improvement across CMHC's technology platforms.

- A strong hands-on experience designing and developing Dynamics 365 solutions, including configuration, customization, plugins, and system integrations.
- A solid understanding of cloud and distributed application principles, including scalability, reliability, security, and performance.
- A demonstrated experience acting as a Subject Matter Expert, providing technical guidance and mentorship while helping establish and enforce development best practices.
- An experience working in Agile environments and solving complex technical problems across multiple systems.
- Strong interpersonal and leadership competencies, including teamwork, facilitation, communication, stakeholder engagement, presentation, influencing, and negotiation skills.

- A strong proficiency in C# and .NET for developing CRM extensions, APIs, backend services, and integration components.
- A strong experience developing Azure solutions using services such as Azure Functions, Logic Apps, App Services, Service Bus, Storage, Key Vault, and API Management.
- Experience designing and implementing REST APIs, asynchronous integrations, event-driven solutions, and serverless architectures.
- A good experience with web development technologies including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
- Experience with Azure DevOps, including CI/CD pipelines, Git workflows, automated builds, testing, and deployment automation.
- Experience with SQL and relational database management systems.
It would be great if you also had:
- Microsoft Dynamics 365 or Power Platform certifications.
- Microsoft Azure certifications.
- Experience integrating Dynamics 365 with D365 Finance & Operations or other enterprise platforms.
- Experience with modern automated testing practices for both Dynamics and .NET/Azure solutions.
- Bilingualism in English and French.

title: Database Administrator
employer: Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada
description:
Language requirements: English or French essential
Special posting considerations:
The intent of the process is to staff one (1) position through a term, an assignment, a secondment agreement, or the Build Canada Exchange program and, to create a pool of partially qualified candidate that may be used to staff similar term or indeterminate positions within NSERC and SSHRC.
Preference will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents.
Who we are
This position falls within a directorate that provides common services to two funding agencies: the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) and Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC).
The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) is Canada’s largest funder of science and engineering. A career at NSERC means supporting the visionaries, explorers and innovators who are searching for the scientific and technical breakthroughs that will advance knowledge, improve the lives of Canadians and transform the world for the better.
At the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC), we bring together the research community, as well as the public, private and not-for-profit sectors, in contributing knowledge, talent and expertise to build a better future for Canada and the world. SSHRC is seeking talented professionals passionate about Canadian research and the value it brings to society.
Visit our career page at NSERC or SSHRC to learn more about why you should join our agency.
What you will do
We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Database Administrator (DBA) to join our Information Technology team. The successful candidate will be responsible for the administration, maintenance, security, performance, and availability of enterprise database environments.
This role supports critical business applications, Business Intelligence (BI) initiatives, legacy systems, and time-sensitive award competition processes. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, demonstrates strong problem-solving skills, and can effectively manage competing priorities while meeting strict deadlines.
What you need to succeed
Education
- Graduation from a recognized post-secondary institution in computer science, information technology, or another field relevant to the position being staffed, or an acceptable combination of education, training, and/or experience.
- MS Azure certifications. (an asset)
- MS SQL Server certifications. (an asset)
- Foreign Credential Validation against Canadian Standards
Experience
- Experience administering, monitoring, maintaining, and optimizing MS SQL Server or Sybase database environments, including capacity planning, performance tuning, and troubleshooting.
- Experience designing, developing, and maintaining database structures and code, including tables, views, stored procedures, functions, triggers, indexes, and DDL/DML scripts.
- Experience implementing and maintaining database security and lifecycle management practices, including access controls, encryption, auditing, vulnerability management, patching, upgrades, and security updates. (an asset)
- Experience managing database availability and recoverability through backup, recovery, disaster recovery, and business continuity procedures. (an asset)
Knowledge
- Knowledge of Azure cloud database services and cloud-based database environments.
- Knowledge of data migration, data conversion, ETL processes, and system integrations, including practices to ensure data integrity, accuracy, and consistency throughout data transition activities.
- Knowledge of data warehousing, reporting, and analytics solutions, including query optimization, reporting performance, and operational documentation
- Knowledge of Sybase and legacy database environments, including the support and maintenance of legacy database systems and applications. (an asset)
- Knowledge of DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure automation. (an asset)
- Knowledge of enterprise database architecture and operations, including high availability, reliability, performance, security, and Azure SQL database modernization initiatives. (an asset)
Competencies
- Communicate effectively (verbal and written)
- Planning and Organizing
- Analysis and Problem Solving
- Adaptability & Priority Management
- Initiative & Action Oriented
- Team oriented
- Client Services oriented
What we offer
Hybrid Work
Our hybrid work model facilitates flexibility, collaboration and work-life balance. We currently require employees to work from our offices 3 days a week (may be subject to change based on operational requirements), while ensuring that the needs of people who may require accommodations, are met in accordance with the Accommodation Policy.
Excellent benefits
In addition to the excellent benefits provided by the federal government, you will also enjoy benefits unique to NSERC/SSHRC, including an annual office closure between December 25 and January 1 to support rest and spending time with family and friends over the holiday season.
Equity, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to inclusive and barrier-free recruitment to create a workforce that reflects the Canadians we serve. We promote employment equity and encourage you to indicate if you belong to one of the designated groups when you apply.
We welcome all candidates, and encourage applications from women, Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Métis and Inuit), veterans, persons with disabilities, Black and other racialized persons, persons of ethnic origins, diverse religions, abilities, sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions, and members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community.
Accommodation
Let our team know if you require accommodation or support during the recruitment process by contacting us at recruiting@nserc-crsng.gc.ca .
What you need to know
- The intention of this process is to establish a pool of partially and fully qualified candidates that may be used to staff indeterminate or term positions at NSERC and SSHRC.
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents.
- A written examination may be administered.
- This position falls within a directorate that provides common services to two funding agencies: the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) and the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC).
We wish to thank all applicants for their interest in applying for this position. Acknowledgment of receipt of applications will be sent to all applicants however, only candidates selected for exams or interviews will be contacted.
If you have technical difficulties when applying for this position, please contact the Njoyn Support Team by email at candidate.njoynhelp@cgi.com or by calling 1-877-427-7717.
If you require additional information on the position, please contact us at recruiting@nserc-crsng.gc.ca .

description:

Data Scientist, Economics & AI
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
What you need to know
We are seeking a Data Scientist with expertise in economics, quantitative modelling, and emerging AI technologies to support economic research, policy analysis, and data-driven decision-making at the Bank of Canada. You will apply data science, machine learning (ML), artificial intelligence (AI), and quantitative methods to challenging economic and research problems, helping economists and researchers make effective use of modern analytical techniques and technologies.
Reporting to the Assistant Director, Data Science, within the Department of Data and Digital Services (DDS), you will work at the intersection of economics, data science, and emerging technologies. Working closely with economists, researchers, business clients, and technology teams, you will develop analytical solutions, AI-enabled tools, and quantitative models that improve research, forecasting, policy analysis, and decision-making.
This role offers an opportunity to apply modern data science and AI approaches to meaningful economic and policy problems while contributing to the development of reusable analytical capabilities. You will work on high-impact initiatives, experiment with emerging methods and technologies, and help modernize analytical and research workflows across the organization.
What you will do
As a Data Scientist, you will contribute to analytical initiatives that support economic research, forecasting, policy analysis, and evidence-based decision-making. Drawing on your knowledge of economics, quantitative methods, and data science, you will work across the analytical lifecycle to develop practical, high-quality solutions.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Designing, developing, testing, and implementing statistical, econometric, ML, and AI models to address economic, research, and policy questions.
- Developing AI-enabled applications, analytical tools, reusable components, and data products that improve research, modelling, forecasting, and analytical workflows.
- Applying LLMs, generative AI, and emerging AI approaches to practical research and analytical use cases, including prototyping, experimentation, evaluation, and implementation.
- Working with structured and unstructured data, including preparing, transforming, validating, exploring, and analyzing datasets for modelling and research.
- Collaborating with economists, researchers, business stakeholders, and technology teams to understand analytical needs and translate them into effective data science solutions.
- Communicating analytical findings, methodologies, assumptions, limitations, and results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Applying sound practices for reproducible research, model validation, responsible AI, explainability, documentation, and analytical quality.
- Exploring and evaluating emerging AI, ML, and analytical techniques and applying them where they can improve economic analysis, research methods, forecasting, or productivity.
What you need to succeed
You are a collaborative and curious data scientist who enjoys using quantitative methods and technology to solve challenging analytical problems. You combine strong technical skills with an understanding of economic and research contexts and can translate analytical questions into practical solutions.
You are comfortable working independently on complex assignments while collaborating closely with economists, researchers, data scientists, and technology specialists. You are an analytical problem solver and continuous learner who can adapt methods and tools as technologies and research needs evolve.
You bring:
- Hands-on experience designing and delivering econometric and economic models using statistical, ML, and AI techniques to support economic research, policy analysis, forecasting, and other quantitative applications.
- Strong knowledge of quantitative methods, with experience in areas such as econometrics, forecasting, statistical modelling, machine learning, or AI.
- Experience applying large language models (LLMs), generative AI, or other emerging AI technologies to analytical, research, or decision-support use cases.
- Proficiency with programming languages or analytical computing environments such as Python, MATLAB, R, or similar tools.
- Experience working with modern analytics platforms such as Azure, Databricks, or equivalent environments.
- Experience working across the data science lifecycle, including data preparation, exploration, modelling, evaluation, and implementation.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to explain analytical approaches and results to technical and non-technical audiences.
Nice-to-Have
Experience in one or more of the following areas:
- Economic research, forecasting, policy analysis, or quantitative economic modelling.
- Time-series analysis, econometric estimation, or simulation methods.

title: AI Safety Lab Lead (#25409)
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2025 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
Are you passionate about safe and responsible AI? Do you want to be part of a pioneering team shaping how AI systems are evaluated, measured, and deployed safely? Do you want your work to have a real impact for Canada and Canadians? If so, we want to meet you! We are seeking a mid‑career RCO‑04 to establish and lead the NRC’s AI Safety Lab, a new capability funded by the Canadian AI Safety Institute (CAISI) and dedicated to evaluating the safety of advanced AI systems. You will be part of a pioneering team conducting rigorous AI safety evaluations and translating technical results into actionable tools, guidance, and recommendations for AI practitioners and policymakers across government and beyond.
Under the guidance of the Principal Advisor for AI Safety, and as part of the Chief Digital Research Officer’s team, you will play a central role in building and operating a scalable AI safety evaluation infrastructure. In collaboration with leading experts from our Digital Technologies Research Centre, you will design, execute, and monitor advanced evaluations at scale on frontier AI models, and contribute to cutting‑edge AI safety research carried out by the NRC in collaboration with CAISI partners nationally and internationally.
Key Responsibilities include:
- Establish and manage a multidisciplinary team of AI safety specialists forming the lab.
- Build and leverage state-of-the-art model evaluation infrastructure and frameworks.
- Work with AI safety researchers from the NRC and CAISI partners in designing, running and documenting AI safety evaluations.
- Establish and steward standardized, reproducible safety evaluation protocols.
- Develop and curate new AI safety benchmarks.
- Translate technical findings into practical solutions and advice, such as new tools for evaluators/developers, or recommendations to policy makers.
The ideal candidate would have:
- A track record of building and managing AI teams.
- Hands-on experience evaluating frontier AI models using safety evaluation frameworks (e.g., Inspect, Moonshot).
- A strong background in compute cluster operations and scalable ML infrastructure.
- Experience designing reproducible evaluation protocols and benchmarks.
- Experience translating research into practical tools, guidance, or policy recommendations.
- The ability to collaborate across research, government, and international partners.
- Strong analytical judgment and initiative.
- Clear communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Master’s degree from a recognized university in Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science or Engineering, or closely related to the position.
Equivalency
In lieu of a master degree, a combination of a Bachelor’s degree with at least 2 years of directly relevant professional experience in applied AI or AI evaluation may be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
You must meet the essential experience criteria and at least two of the Specialised Experience to move forward in this process.
Essential Experience
- Recent* experience leading or managing technical teams in an AI/ML, data analytics, or digital technologies environment.
- Recent* experience evaluating, benchmarking, or red-teaming AI models (open-source or closed-source) or AI systems.
- Experience in managing AI/ML or data analytics projects for government or industry clients.
- Experience developing Python-based tooling and automation for ML/AI workflows.
- Experience in documenting experimental AI results through technical reports, internal documentation, or scientific publications.
*Recent is defined as within the last 3 years.
Specialised Experience
- Experience with red-teaming workflows, adversarial testing, or stress-testing of AI systems (including agentic systems).
- Experience with compute clusters and job orchestration (e.g., SLURM).
- Experience with ML experiment tracking tools (e.g., MLflow, Weights & Biases).
- Experience developing or curating AI benchmark datasets and associated documentation (e.g., through HuggingFace).
- Experience translating AI research into practical tools, guidance, or policy recommendations.
- Experience conducting AI projects with researchers or through international collaboration.
Condition of employment
Secret clearance
A thorough security clearance process will be applied.
For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.
Language requirements
Bilingual Imperative CBC/CBC
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Ability to lead the development of reproducible evaluation protocols and benchmarks for frontier AI models and systems.
- Ability to communicate complex technical findings clearly to researchers, government stakeholders, and policy audiences.
- Knowledge of AI safety concepts, risk taxonomies, or governance frameworks (e.g., TBS guidelines, NIST AI Risk Management Framework) and their connection to technical evaluation.
- Ability to design and oversee scalable AI evaluation infrastructure across on-premises and cloud environments.
- Knowledge of AI safety evaluation frameworks (e.g., Inspect AI, Moonshot) and their application to frontier model assessment.
- Ability to make sound technical decisions when configuring evaluations across different model types, balancing compute budgets, reproducibility, and result validity.
- Ability to manage and prioritize competing technical workstreams across a multidisciplinary team.
- Knowledge of agentic AI architectures and how design choices such as tool access, memory, and planning affect safety-relevant behaviours.
- Ability to design experiment tracking and data management workflows that support reproducibility across multiple researchers and evaluation campaigns.
Behavioural competencies
- Research - Communication (Level 3)
- Research - Results orientation (Level 3)
- Supervisor - Client focus (Level 2)
- Supervisor - Teamwork (Level 3)
- Supervisor - Organizational/environmental awareness (Level 2)
- Management services - Conceptual and analytical ability (Level 3)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile(s): Management Services ; Research ; Supervisor
View all competency profiles
Compensation
This position is classified as a Research Council Officer (RCO), a group that is unique to the NRC. The intent of this hiring action is to staff this position at the RCO-3 to RCO-4 level, which is a mid-career level position with a salary range of $119,688 to $168,192 .
NOTE: Please note that the full RO/RCO salary scale has five levels. Salary determination will be based on a review of the candidate’s expertise, outcomes and impacts of their previous work experience relative to the requirements of the level. As such, the initial salary could be within another level of the RO/RCO salary scale (i.e. above or below the intended level for this position).
In addition, the incumbent will receive the Bilingualism Bonus of $800 per year.
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
​
Notes
- Relocation assistance will be determined in accordance with the NRC's directives.
- ​A pre-qualified list may be established for similar positions for a one year period.
- Preference will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents of Canada. Please include citizenship information in your application.
- The incumbent must adhere to safe workplace practices at all times.
- We thank all those who apply, however only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

About the position
Duties
Reporting to the Director, Research and Innovation, the Technical Leader, Engineering applies expert knowledge in providing advice to Commissioners and CER staff with respect to pipeline integrity, safety and related engineering and management system aspects of oil and gas pipeline systems. This includes providing advice and support in the development and execution of integrity-related compliance and enforcement activities, such as inspections, compliance meetings, management system audits, application assessment and incident investigations.
Working closely with the Professional Leader, Engineer, the Technical Leader provides technical coaching to staff and participates actively in the professional development of engineers-in-training, engineers, and technical specialists.
The Technical Leader regularly scans the external environment and monitors internal activities, to stay abreast of emerging issues of interest to the organization, and to influence the organization to take pro-active actions regarding emerging issues. The incumbent would be an active participant in external committees such as CSA standards technical committees, the International Pipeline Conference, and the Banff Pipeline Workshop, and would cooperate with organizations such as CanmetMATERIALS (CANMET), Canadian regulators and international regulators such as the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA).
The Technical Leader is occasionally required to conduct field inspections, audits, or site visits in remote areas and will be required to obtain the CER Inspection Officer designation within a reasonable timeframe.

The position is based in Calgary Alberta

The Canada Energy Regulator (CER) helps keep energy moving safely across Canada by reviewing projects, sharing energy information, and upholding world-class safety and environmental standards. Employment at Parliament not only opens doors to professional growth and skill enhancement, it also fosters a deep sense of pride and accomplishment as a valued member of our workforce.

Lock/Bridge Operator I (GL-MOC-05) Parks Canada careers: where passion meets purpose . You might be wondering why you would come to work for the Parks Canada Agency? To join a team of passionate people who care about the protection and presentation of Canada’s outstanding natural and cultural resources through a system of national parks, national marine conservation areas and national historic sites in all regions of Canada. Parks Canada is a federal government agency responsible for the protection and presentation of Canada’s outstanding natural and cultural resources through a system of national parks, national marine conservation areas and national historic sites in all regions of Canada. The Quebec Waterways unit manages five historic canals stretching from Montreal to the St. Lawrence, Richelieu and Outaouais rivers. These canals are situated in three important tourism regions in the province and also have numerous collaborations with important stakeholders and partners. • Carillon Canal National Historic Site • Chambly Canal National Historic Site • Lachine Canal National Historic Site • Saint-Ours Canal National Historic Site • Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue Canal National Historic Site ⏰ Closing date: November 30, 2026 - 11:59 p.m., Eastern Time We encourage you to submit your application promptly, as applications may be reviewed on an ongoing basis. The work of a lock and bridge attendant requires rigor, resourcefulness, and good physical fitness. You will be responsible for operating locks and/or bridges*, maintaining grounds, structures and equipment, and providing courteous service to users in accordance with Parks Canada standards. The position is physically demanding and mainly works outside (more than 10 hours a day, exposure to sun, rain and bad weather). You will walk long distances on various terrains, use stairs or ladders and could lift loads up to 20 kg. Your main tasks: Paint, clean, weed, mow, empty bins and maintain sanitary facilities. Use various tools and equipment (lawnmower, pressure washer, drill, boat, golf cart, etc.). Perform certain administrative tasks using computer tools. *The locks of the Canal-de-Chambly have mechanisms that are operated manually. Join us and contribute concretely to the functioning of Quebec’s waterways, while working in a unique natural environment! Who we are
The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) is Canada’s largest funder of science and engineering. A career at NSERC means supporting the visionaries, explorers and innovators who are searching for the scientific and technical breakthroughs that will advance knowledge, improve the lives of Canadians and transform the world for the better.
Visit our career page at NSERC to learn more about why you should join our agency.
What you will do
The Deputy Director is providing the focal point for the Division’s corporate secretariat operations, governance and compliance activities; ensuring delivery of corporate operations, legislative and policy compliance of the organization; developing and maintaining frameworks related to governance, Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP), funding eligibility and terms & conditions; coordinating special projects and studies and consulting widely with internal and external stakeholders to inform decision-making. The Deputy Director is the second in command for corporate secretariat operations and is acting for the Executive Director in their absence.
What you need to succeed
Education
- A university degree from a recognized post-secondary institution, or an acceptable combination of education, training and experience relevant to the position.
- Foreign Credential Validation against Canadian Standards .
Experience
- Experience in interpreting legislation and regulations, and in applying government policies, standards and guidelines.
- Experience in providing policy advice, support and services to senior management and corporate governance.
- Experience in applying privacy legislation, policy and directives.
- Experience in managing projects and processes involving multiple parties, both external and internal.
- Experience in supervising staff and consultants.
Knowledge
- Knowledge of the Government of Canada scientific, research and innovation priorities, initiatives and programs aimed at building research and scientific excellence in order to develop plans, policy and policy positions and provide advice that is in line with the federal direction.
- Knowledge of the broad research environment and issues in Canada, as well as globally, including the university, government and/or private sector contexts, the changing requirements of Canadian research ecosystem, and diversity considerations, in order to manage issues, conduct research and develop recommendations on funding policies.
- Knowledge of government planning, risk management and accountability policies, guidelines and reporting requirements, and a range of policies and regulations and federal legislation applicable to NSERC and to research.
- Knowledge of the Access to Information Act, the Privacy Act, the Financial Administration Act, and a range of Treasury Board Secretariat and other policies and regulations (e.g., Transfer Payment Policy for Grants and Contributions) related to policy and program development, strategic planning, and governing managerial/corporate functions.
Key Leadership Competencies
- Create Vision and Strategy.
- Mobilize People.
- Uphold Integrity and Respect.
- Collaboration with Partners and Stakeholders.
- Promote Innovation and Guide Change.
- Achieve Results.
Equity, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to inclusive and barrier-free recruitment to create a workforce that reflects the Canadians we serve. We promote employment equity and encourage you to indicate if you belong to one of the designated groups when you apply.
We welcome all candidates, and encourage applications from women, Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Métis and Inuit), veterans, persons with disabilities, Black and other racialized persons, persons of ethnic origins, diverse religions, abilities, sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions, and members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community.
