title: Research Officer - Construction Productivity & Optimization (#26191)
description:
Language requirements: English essential
The role
NRC Construction is implementing the “Platform to Decarbonize the Construction Sector at Scale” (NRC Platform) to accelerate and scale up new technologies to help transition the Canadian construction sector towards decarbonization and contribute to the emerging low-carbon economy. It will also establish new codes, standards, specifications, and guidelines to position the sector to achieve its 2050 greenhouse gas (GHG) carbon reduction targets. These investments will help spur the growth of Canada’s clean technology sector and help achieve Canada’s international commitments to reduce GHG emissions.
Federal Budget 2022 proposed that the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) receive $183.2 million over seven years (2022-29) to transition the Canadian construction sector towards decarbonization and enhanced productivity. The funding will support the implementation of a NRC Platform consisting of three integrated and synergistic Programs to advance the transformation of Canada’s construction sector and contribute to the emerging low-carbon economy.
The Digitalization and Productivity Challenge Program (approximately $70M over seven years) will drive transformation to digitalized and automated construction and accelerate the adoption of novel off-site construction methodologies. The program will support lower construction time and cost, while improving sector innovation potential, productivity and the pace at which low-carbon solutions can be deployed in new and retrofit construction projects.
The program will be specifically designed to harness and focus Canada’s research and innovation capacity in industry, academia and research-based OGDs to fill key knowledge gaps (e.g. guidelines, standard methods of data exchange, standards development, integration of off-site manufacturing design and practices for deconstruction, productivity quantification, among others) to realize the potential benefits of off-site construction and automation. It will seek to implement processes to optimize the designs and compliance of buildings and infrastructure, leverage benefits of advanced manufacturing processes including modular off-site construction (MOC), and advance development of low-carbon retrofit solutions that lever performance-based design.
The role (continued)
Research and development motivated by this program will provide the technical solutions needed for early adopters in the private sector to uniformly implement integrated digital construction practices throughout the asset lifecycle and across the sector. Demonstration projects with early adopters will showcase the value of digitalized construction solutions, which will help increase sector productivity, reduce time and cost, when coupled with a shift from prescriptive to performance-based solutions.
The primary responsibility of the RO is to support the goals of NRC’s Platform to Decarbonize the Construction Sector at Scale, and other Programs served by the Intelligent Building Operations unit. These goals require research of international calibre and the development and application of advanced technologies to support the needs of our numerous industry partners. The RO works in a team environment with researchers and technical experts in world-class facilities. Activities also include the development of proposals for new research initiatives, effective project management, support to the enhancement of facilities, and communication of research plans and results to stakeholders.
Screening criteria

Education
A PhD in Construction Management or Industrial Engineering with an emphasis on Construction Value Chain.
A PhD in a related field, combined with significant experience in measuring and analyzing construction productivity/efficiency or related research may also be considered.
Education related to construction supply chain valuation, life cycle environmental and/or cost assessment maybe considered an asset.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Experience in conducting research on construction productivity and/or conducting comparative studies on productivity/performance data to enhance construction productivity (time, cost, environmental impacts) through applications such as MOC, IPD, BIM or other construction practices. Experience related to comparative analysis of MOC vs conventional construction may be considered an asset.
- Experience in construction supply chain logistics/network optimization, including areas such as transportation systems, operations research, or stochastic optimization.
- Experience in research proposal development, working with diverse stakeholders and multi-disciplinary teams, project execution, documentation, and reporting.
Experience in construction (on-site and/or off-site) automation (e.g. automated data acquisition, automated collision avoidance, automated manufacturing technologies and processes may be considered an asset.
Experience in business development, marketing activities, and/or the development of partnerships and collaborations may be considered an asset.

- Ability to apply knowledge to research and technology development projects. Knowledge in leading/participating in research project planning, work scheduling, costing, proposal development, and engaging with stakeholders.
- Advanced knowledge in construction performance measurement frameworks and metrics focusing on productivity improvement and/or carbon reduction.
- Advanced knowledge of productivity enhancements and/or emissions reductions through non-conventional construction practices such as leveraging MOC, IPD, Digital Tools/Solutions, AI.
- Knowledge of comparison research for construction performance and productivity of:
- different construction practices, technologies, processes, and/or materials; and/or planned vs actual outputs.
Knowledge in benchmarking construction performance and productivity may be considered an asset.

The payments landscape in Canada and globally is evolving rapidly, driven by technological advancements that are introducing innovative ways for consumers and businesses to make payments. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), the Bank of Canada is responsible for registering retail payment service providers (PSPs) that perform retail payment activities, maintaining a public registry of PSPs, and supervising PSPs’ compliance with operational risk management, fund safeguarding and reporting requirements.
What you will do
As a Senior Supervisor in the Risk Supervision team, you will play a crucial role in shaping the Bank’s retail payments supervisory framework in a fast-paced and dynamic environment. Being at the forefront of Canada’s rapidly evolving payments landscape, you will strengthen resilience and help protect the integrity of the payments ecosystem.
You will apply your knowledge of cyber and information security risk management practices to help implement the Bank’s framework for PSP supervision, and assess the compliance of PSPs with their regulatory obligations.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Assessing PSPs' cyber and information security risks,vulnerabilities, and control effectiveness
- Analyzing PSP reporting related to cyber and information security incidents
- Communicating with PSPs on ongoing risk assessment activities
- Collaborating with colleagues on supervisory assessments and actions
- Developing and maintaining business documentation and information repositories
- Contributing to the development of processes and policies to optimize the Bank’s approach to PSP risk supervision
What you need to succeed
As a self-motivated critical thinker, you have the following industry knowledge and experience:
- Cybersecurity principles and risk experience Strong understanding of cyber security principles and risk management practices Knowledge of cyber defence mechanisms and industry best practices. Experience assessing, managing or supervising cybersecurity practices, ideally in regulatory , consulting or second or third line of defence roles. Strong theoretical and practical knowledge of IT and cyber risk including risk identification evaluation and mitigation. Understanding of risk management frameworks such as the NIST cybersecurity framework, ISO 27001 etc.
- Cybersecurity landscape awareness Solid understanding of emerging cybersecurity threats, trends, and leading practices
- Regulatory compliance knowledge Understanding critical financial sector regulations and frameworks (such as PCI DSS, SOC 2, GDPR, PIPEDA, RPAA) and their implications for cyber security and risk management.
- Cyber tools knowledge Familiarity with tools used for risk management, incident response and monitoring .
You are able to synthesize complex information and provide high quality analysis while considering multiple factors and perspectives often within contexts of ambiguity and evolving information.
You are flexible and able to adapt to an evolving work environment and changing priorities. Furthermore, you are able to organize and balance a variety of tasks. You have a proven ability to communicate clearly and adapt your communication style for a wide range of audiences, including senior management and external stakeholders.
You are equally comfortable working collaboratively within a team, or independently. You develop and maintain harmonious relationships with a wide range of business contacts and build supportive working relationships with peers, your leader, as well as internal and external stakeholders.
Nice-to-have
- Knowledge of incident management and response processes.
- Knowledge of cloud technologies and cloud security practices and understanding how they apply to risk management and cybersecurity within cloud environments.
- Understanding of secure system architecture and design principles .
- Knowledge of DevOps or DevSecOps practices
- Familiarity with retail payment services, the retail payments ecosystem, or financial technology companies (paytechs or fintechs)
- Strong interest in supervisory technology, including artificial intelligence to support efficient supervisory practices
- At least one of the following certifications: CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional) CISM (Certified Information Security Manager) CRISC (Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control) CGRC (Certified Governance, Risk and Compliance) CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor)
Your education
The position requires:
- a masters degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity or a related discipline, with at least five years of relevant experience; or
- a minimum bachelors degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity or a related discipline, with at least six years of relevant experience.
A combination of education and experience may be considered. Candidates with degrees in other fields may be considered where they demonstrate significant practical cybersecurity experience.
Innovative Mindset We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement
The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.

Hybrid Work Model The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.

title: Research Librarian
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Company Description
The Library of Parliament is a non-partisan organization that provides a unique and stimulating work environment. We are led by our guiding principles of agility, collaboration, excellence, impartiality, and inclusion. For more information about the Library and what we offer, visit Employment opportunities at the Library of Parliament .
Job Description
Reporting to the Manager, Library Branches, or Senior Manager, Integrated Reference Services, the Research Librarians provide timely, reliable and authoritative reference services on a wide range of topics in person, over the phone and by email. Working with multi-disciplinary teams, they respond to reference requests from parliamentarians, including members of the House of Commons, senators, parliamentary associations or delegations, and other parliamentary clients. They have the opportunity to work on various client-focused initiatives as well as substantive research inquiries covering a wide variety of subjects. The work they do helps parliamentarians to develop legislation that will shape Canada’s future and to serve their constituents.
The incumbent performs the following duties:
- Provides high-quality, timely, accurate, non-partisan and confidential information in both official languages.
- Provides in-person services at Library service points.
- Provides orientation and instruction to clients in the use of Library collections, tools, products and services, and promotes Library products and services through meetings, guided tours for visitors and dignitaries, presentations, information sessions and marketing activities.
- Develops and maintains expertise in parliamentary and current affairs, including parliamentary procedure and administration, internal and external print and electronic collections, core online systems, and the Library’s products and services.
- Develops and maintains professional expertise in library and information studies.
Qualifications
Education :
- A Master of Library and Information Science (MLIS) or a Master of Information Studies (MIS) degree from an institution accredited by the American Library Association (ALA) or from a recognized accrediting body deemed equivalent by the ALA.
- Applicants who anticipate graduating in the winter or summer semesters of 2027 may be considered.
Experience :
- Experience conducting in-depth searches using print and online sources.
- Experience providing written responses to requests for information.
- Experience in client-facing positions.
Knowledge :
- Knowledge of reference resources, online search tools and search techniques.
Competencies :
- Adaptability
- Client Focus
- Embracing Diversity
- Exemplifying Integrity
- Organizational Awareness
- Data / Information Retrieval and Analysis
- Quality focus
- Communication
- Teamwork
- Analytical Thinking
Asset Criteria :
- Experience in legislative, government or special libraries.
- Knowledge of online search tools and reference sources relevant to Canadian politics and current affairs.
- Knowledge of Canada’s system of government, parliamentary institutions and government departments.
Operational Requirements :
- Research Librarians may be required to work an evening duty shift every four to five weeks (when the House of Commons or the Senate are sitting). These hours are from 10:30 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.
Conditions of Employment :
- A successful pre-employment security screening.

The Library of Parliament welcomes all candidates to apply and encourages applications from Indigenous persons, racialized persons, 2SLGBTQIA+ persons and persons with disabilities for this position.

title: Collections Agent
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
About the role
Join the Commercial Solutions team, in the Collections Agent position. In this role, you will administer a portfolio of judgment and non-judgment debt owed to CMHC by assessing and processing the settlement of insurance claims resulting from mortgage and non-mortgage defaults related to government programs while minimizing risk to achieve maximum collection on a case-by-case basis and a minimum of client complaints.
This is a temporary position of a duration of 12 months with possibility of renewal.
What you'll do:
- Examine financial information, seeking historical and contextual information from a variety of sources and establish the deficiency balance.
- Review Bankruptcies Proposals to protect CMHC's rights to obtain the highest possible dividends and to determine whether the proposal will be accepted or opposed.
- Perform analysis of different legal actions and or judgment renewals to be taken when a settlement is not reached.
- Recommend legal remedies to supervisor and solicitors, which include placing execution orders against the client's additional properties, conducting debt examinations, garnishment orders, alias writs, foreclosures, power of sales and bankruptcies.
- Provide documentation to senior team members for review and approval, as and when necessary, to ensure management of risk when faced with exceptions on policy or procedure outside financial authority level.
- Locate consumers by tracing, using various resources and tools (such as credit bureau, underwriting system (emiliRU), mainframe, social media, internet platforms, Canada411, LinkedIn, etc.).
- Negotiate settlement directly with clients to reach the best possible arrangement within delegated authority limits, referring complex or disputed claims to senior team members for resolution.
- Provide guidance to third-party collection agencies, service providers, approved lenders and other internal departments such as claims, multi-units, underwriting, loans administration including legal actions, settlements and settlements in lieu of the judgment as well as explanations for CMHC's position.
What you should have:
- A post-secondary education in a related field such as business, accounting, finance, legal, or commerce.
- A minimum of three years of prior relevant experience in a customer service and/or collections environment.
- An understanding of the competitive mortgage industry environment and the mortgage insurance business.
- A strong knowledge of the National Housing Act, Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act as well as the Creditors Relief Act, Estate Administration, and Collection Provincial Legislation.
- Strong oral and written communication skills including negotiating skills.
- The ability to exercise empathy, diplomacy and tact with the ability to diffuse emotionally distraught and irate debtors.
- Strong organizational skills including the ability to multi-task, prioritize, meet deadlines and take initiative.
- Analytical and problem-solving skills including the application of sound judgment and the ability to escalate.
It would be great if you also had:
- Experience working with accounts where misrepresentation or fraud has occurred.
- Good knowledge of mortgage financing and real estate laws, collections, default remedy and/or property administration.

- Proficiency in Python for model development, data analysis and automation; working knowledge of R and/or SAS.
- Knowledge of model risk management concepts, governance frameworks and validation best practices.
- A good understanding of the Canadian financial sector, real estate markets and the mortgage ecosystem.
- Excellent analytical, written communication and presentation skills.
It would be great if you also had:
- Strong actuarial and quantitative foundation, including a solid understanding of mathematical finance, risk management, pricing principles and actuarial methodologies.
- An actuarial or risk management designation (FCIA, FSA, FRM, PRM or equivalent) or significant progress toward one.
- Knowledge of large language models (LLMs) and agentic AI frameworks, along with their practical applications in financial services, as well as hands-on experience with generative AI (GenAI) tools and big data ecosystems (e.g., Hadoop, HDFS, Hive, Spark).
- An experience working in a regulatory environment or with OSFI supervisory processes.

title: Technical Officer, Electromechanical Prototyping for Medical Devices Research (#25967)
description:
Language requirements: English or French essential
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are looking for a Technical Officer to join us. We are a 5-person multidisciplinary engineering team which provides technical support for research and development of Lab-on-a-Chip devices and systems. We design and build the electronic, optical, pneumatic and mechanical control components and platforms needed to automate microfluidic systems that perform rapid analyses of clinically relevant biological targets. We operate within NRC’s Bioanalytical Micro-Nano Devices Section, which is composed of more than 35 researchers and technical officers with a unique combination of expertise spanning physics, engineering, chemistry, molecular biology, and cellular biology. The position, located at the NRC facilities in Boucherville, Quebec, will require the candidate to perform electronic circuit prototyping, printed circuit board design, electronic and mechanical assembly and simple mechanical prototyping. The work will be performed within existing systems, so will involve microcontroller-based electronics, motors and motion controllers, low pressure pneumatic systems, data logging systems and various data/image processing systems and techniques. The individual will need to be creative and versatile to contribute technically in multiple areas of expertise. They will have to recognize and solve problems associated with experimental or analytical techniques, write documentation, develop fabrication and assembly procedures, and actively support quality management systems. The selected candidate is expected to be able to work independently as well as part of the broader R&D team in an environment requiring a high-level of adaptability and multitasking.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, electronics engineering, physics engineering or mechatronics engineering. Related technical degrees (such as electrical engineering technician) combined with experience related to the position may be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
Recent experience with the following is required:
- Design of electronic circuits and circuit boards with professional EDA software (4 years or more)
- Assembly and testing of printed circuit boards and cabling
- Design, manufacturing and assembly of simple mechanical parts (at least hobby-level mechanical design and 3D printing)
Experience with one or more of following may be considered an asset:
- Circuit design in Altium
- Architecting, designing and implementing multi-component software/embedded systems
- Integrating hardware with software
- Use of collaborative development tools such as Git
- Programming for FPGA and/or microcontrollers (C/C++)
- Programming application software in Python
- Experience working in a team-based, multi-disciplinary research environment
- Experience in the field of medical devices or related research and development
Condition of employment
Reliability Status
For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
English or French
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Design of electronic circuits and circuit boards
- Electronic assembly and testing of proto-boards, PCBs and cabling
- Mechanical assembly to support electronic testing
- Troubleshooting the integration of hardware and software
The following competencies are considered assets:
- Design of microcontroller-based electronic circuits
- Development of microcontroller firmware
- Use of collaborative development tools, such as Git
Behavioural competencies
- Research Technician/Technologist - Results orientation (Level 2)
- Research Technician/Technologist - Teamwork (Level 2)
- Research Technician/Technologist - Communication (Level 2)
- Research Technician/Technologist - Initiative (Level 2)
- Research Technician/Technologist - Creative thinking (Level 3)
- Research Technician/Technologist - Self-knowing and self-development (Level 2)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Research Technician/Technologist
View all competency profiles
Compensation
From $66,126 to $91,012 per annum.
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Notes
- In 2026, the NRC was chosen as one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, a National Capital Region Top Employer and Forbes Canada’s Best Employer.
- Relocation assistance will be determined in accordance with the NRC's directives.
- A pre-qualified list may be established for similar positions for a one-year period.
- Preference will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents of Canada. Please include citizenship information in your application.
- The incumbent must adhere to safe workplace practices at all times.
- We thank all those who apply, however only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

description:

Who can apply: All persons who have legal status to work in Canada. Please indicate in your application the reason for which you are entitled to work in Canada: Canadian Citizenship, permanent resident status, or work permit.
About the position
Duties
You provide visitors with opportunities to discover, appreciate and learn about the Park and its natural and/or cultural resources and understand their significance to Canada. Leading guided hikes to Burgess Shale fossil sites and other hikes that highlight conservation work.
Plans, adapts, develops and leads guided hikes within the field unit.
Work environment
Like to hike in our spectacular mountain parks?
Are you in great physical shape and excited to lead up to four full-day hikes each week?
Are you excited to share stories about Burgess Shale fossils, resource conservation efforts and key Parks messages?
As a guide, you ensure visitors have a safe and memorable experience by facilitating interactive, fun and safe hikes that are challenging full day hikes of up to 22 km with 1000m elevation gain on steep, rocky trails.
Intent of the process
The results of this process will be used to fill anticipated vacancies for 2027 and may be used in the future to fill permanent or temporary vacancies that may arise at the Interpretation Officer II, PM 02, in various locations, with full or part-time hours, for various tenures, such as: Seasonal Indeterminate, Term, Acting Assignment or Assignment at level, depending on status of the selected candidate.

🏆 The Parks Canada team is proud to be recognized by Forbes as one of Canada's Best Employers (2026).

1. When providing your references, please include two to support hiking ability.
2. Individuals who qualified on process 2022-PKS-LLYK-EA-081 and 2023-PKS-LLYK-EA-071 need not apply for this competition.

Additional information on preparing for your interview can be found here: Applying for Government of Canada jobs: Testing and accommodation measures - Canada.ca

• Please provide complete and thorough details of your education and experience.
• Do not assume that the screening board has any previous knowledge of your background, qualifications, or work history. You must be specific and provide concrete examples/details for each Experience element, as applications will be screened only on the information provided.
• Failure to provide sufficient information may result in your application being screened out of the competition.
📢 Our intention is to communicate with candidates via email. Candidates must include in their application a valid email address and ensure this address is functional at all times and accepts messages from unknown users. It is the candidate's responsibility to ensure that any changes to their personal information be provided to the email address indicated on this job advertisement.
Conditions of employment
Must be met prior to the employment offer:
• Obtain and maintain Reliability Status
• Possession and maintenance of a valid Class 5 Driver’s License or provincial equivalent
• Possession and maintenance of valid 40-hour Wilderness First Aid and CPR certification or higher level
• Possession and maintenance of a valid Group Management course certificate (Interpretive Guides Association Guide, Association of Canadian Mountain Guides Hiking Guide, Outdoor Council of Canada, or equivalent)
• Will be required to undergo and pass pre-placement and periodic medical checks
• Ability to do 8-11 hour hikes up steep trails for 4 consecutive days/week in a variety of weather conditions
Operational Requirements
The position requires the incumbent to:

EDUCATION

*Acceptable combination of education, training and experience is defined as:

• Successful completion of a minimum of three (3) courses relevant to the duties of the position (e.g., courses taken through continuing education facilities, colleges, universities, professional or governmental organizations or employers including training provided by Indigenous elders or group that may include but are not limited to courses in heritage interpretation, communications, public speaking, performing arts); AND
• A minimum of 12 months’ experience working in the fields of education, guiding, interpretation, and/or outreach-communications.

EXPERIENCE

• Experience in the delivery of cultural and/or natural heritage programs, including guiding day hikes
• Significant* backcountry hiking within the past two years.
*Significant refers to a minimum of six (6) full day hikes and one (1) multi-day hike in the backcountry per year. In your three references, please include two to support hiking ability.
Applied / assessed at a later date

We are looking for a Technical Officer to support the goals of NRC and Clean Energy Innovation (CEI) Research Centre through research and development and application of advanced technologies. You will be working in a team environment with researchers and technical experts in world-class facilities, while sharing our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The technical officer will provide the technical expertise on techniques/approaches in the fields of mechanical, materials, and electrochemical testing to ensure that project objectives are met in a timely manner. The technical officer will plan and conduct standard tests to determine mechanical, electrochemical and other properties of the materials being tested. The work follows established protocols, but often requires the development of novel methods and modifications to test equipment. The technical officer’s duties include:
- Participate in the development of new capabilities and apparatuses aimed at addressing gaps in materials assessment under hydrogen exposure conditions and/or other environments.
- Participation in a wide range of activities relating to the materials testing and evaluation for clean energy using standard techniques and support the development and implementation of new test capabilities.

- Perform analyses to determine other material properties using a wide variety of analytical tools including, optical and electron microscopy and XRD.
- Collect, compile and provide mechanical interpretation of data, and prepare and install lab equipment based on specifications.
- Involve in coordination of lab or facility resources and is responsible for the maintenance of equipment within their area of responsibility.

About the position
Duties
Positions in the Trade Remedies Investigations Division offer an opportunity to work on some of the most important and fast-moving trade issues facing Canada. Our work supports the CBSA’s mandate while contributing directly to Canada’s economic security, competitiveness and prosperity.
Our mandate is broadly focused on fair trade. The division works across the full spectrum of policy and operations, from setting strategic direction and developing programs and policies, to conducting complex investigations, analyzing industries and markets, and engaging directly with Canadian businesses, stakeholders, foreign governments and international organizations.
At the heart of our work are investigations into unfair trade practices. We examine whether imported goods are being sold in Canada below fair market value or are benefiting from foreign government subsidies, and we administer trade measures that help ensure Canadian producers can compete on a fair and level playing field.
The work is analytical, investigative and highly relevant to the Canadian economy. It brings together financial analysis, accounting, industrial and market knowledge, research, data and judgment to answer complex real-world questions and support consequential decisions.
Work environment
In line with the Treasury Board Secretariat (TBS) Direction on prescribed presence in the workplace, the Canada Border Service Agency (CBSA) has adopted a fixed day approach to support hybrid arrangements for employees to work a minimum of 4 (four) days per week in their designated work location and 1 (one) day per week at their designated telework location, where operationally feasible. Please note, this requirement is subject to change based on any future shift in hybrid work model direction or following change in operational requirements.
For more information, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/government/publicservice/staffing/direction-prescribed-presence-workplace.html
The CBSA is the first point of entry for travellers and goods arriving to Canada. We are, in effect, the face of Canada. The CBSA was established in December 2003. Its creation integrated border functions related to customs, immigration, enforcement, and food, plant, and animal inspection.
The CBSA supports both national security and economic prosperity by preventing the entry of those travelers or goods posing a potential threat to Canada while at the same time facilitating the flow of people and legitimate goods across the borders.
Why work for us? It’s simple. Our mandate is unique. We are a diverse, inclusive and respectful workforce. As one of the largest public service organizations in Canada, we can offer a variety of interesting and challenging opportunities; and we take your professional development to heart.

About the position
Duties
The Grain Inspector Development Program (GIDP) is a unique program, developed and delivered by the CGC that trains individuals to qualify as a working level Grain Inspector. The program can take up to two years to complete, depending on an individual's progress in developing the required competencies. Throughout the program, Grain Inspector Trainees will work a modular curriculum of class work and practical, hands-on working practicum at busy Canadian ports.
Grain Inspector Trainees will learn to:
• perform preliminary inspection and analysis of grain samples;
• grade grain samples;
• draw representative grain samples;
• determine the protein content of wheat;
• maintain records of inspection data;
• inspect equipment;
• perform other related duties as assigned.
Grain Inspector Trainees will be expected to develop the required technical and behavioural competencies within the program as they progress from Trainee (PI-CGC-01) to full working-level Grain Inspector (PI-CGC-03).
Trainees will receive constant monitoring and feedback so individuals may be promoted to the next level as they successfully demonstrate the program’s competency standards and expectations. Trainee progress and success will be dependent on the individual’s own effort and capacity to learn the required competencies rather than a pre-determined schedule.
Trainees will be on probation for the duration of the development program and may be released at any time for failure to meet program expectations and demonstrate the required technical/behavioural competencies. Successful completion of all GIDP components will be a condition of employment for all participants upon acceptance of a Grain Inspector trainee position.
The Grain Inspector Development Program can be the first step towards are warding career in the public service. Though many choose to spend their careers as grain inspectors, there may be opportunities to become an inspection specialist, inspection trainer, supervisor, or manager. There are many ways for graduates to apply their skills and grow well beyond the completion of the program.
Work environment
Grain Inspector Trainees will work in a heavy industrial environment with exposure to moving railcars, automated equipment, dust, noise, bird excrement, heights and rodents. Employees must use personal protective equipment (supplied) as required for safety purposes. Any known allergies must be controlled through the use of masks and/or medication and must not impinge on the trainee’s ability to perform the job.

title: Senior Specialist, Financial Risk Oversight (Capital Markets)
description:
Language requirements: English essential
About the role
Join the CRO’s Securitization and Capital Markets Risks Oversight team, in the Senior Specialist, Financial Risk Oversight (Capital Markets) position. In this role, you will provide independent risk oversight of CMHC’s capital markets and investment activities, drawing on a strong understanding of both their commercial objectives and associated financial risks. You will act as a subject matter expert in areas such as investments (including pension fund and corporate assets), market risk, liquidity risk, capital adequacy, asset-liability management, and counterparty credit risk. This will often require abstract thinking and creating innovative solutions, for example, analysis, templates, etc., where none currently exist. You will translate complex analysis into clear insights and recommendations for senior management and support informed, risk-based decision-making.
What you’ll do:
- Conduct independent oversight to ensure CMHC’s financial risk management and controls are robust and effective.
- Identify, assess, measure, monitor and report on key current and emerging financial risks to the Corporation.
- Employ tools, models, and assessment techniques, including financial statement analysis, data analysis and external environment scanning to assess and measure risk exposure relative to risk appetite and build and maintain forward looking capabilities.
- Develop clear presentations, memos and risk reports synthesizing capital markets and investment matters into key messages and actionable recommendations. Present findings confidently to technical and non-technical audiences.
- Provide support and guidance on risk management frameworks and policies to ensure effective management of risks and controls.
- Identify emerging issues and trends to inform decision-making and develop innovative solutions to complex problems to present to senior management.
- Collaborate with Risk, Business and Finance functions to deliver high-quality outcomes within established accountabilities and timelines.
- Be up to date on regulatory guidance and industry-leading practices, assessing and incorporating them for elevating the quality of risk oversight.
What you should have:
- A degree in finance, accounting, economics or business.
- A minimum of five (5) years of experience in capital markets risk management and risk oversight and reporting or related relevant experience.
- A demonstrated knowledge and expertise in utilizing risk management practices.
- A demonstrated depth in capital markets and investments including strong understanding of financial instruments, capital management, liquidity management and the underlying risk considerations.
- Superior communication and presentation skills with demonstrated expertise in articulating complex concepts to various levels of stakeholders.
- A demonstrated ability to receive and incorporate feedback, align with leadership direction and team priorities, and independently deliver agreed outcomes.
- Bloomberg experience.
It would be great if you also had:
- A professional designation, certification and/or specific training in risk management or financial analysis (e.g., Chartered Financial Analyst, Professional/Certified Risk Manager, Financial Risk Management, Chartered Professional Accountant).
- An experience using quantitative and qualitative techniques, including stress testing, scenario analysis, financial modelling, portfolio analytics or data analysis, to assess current and emerging financial risks. Python and SQL experience.
- Bilingualism in both official languages (English & French).

title: Technical Officer, Facility Leader (#25336)
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!6
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are looking for a Facility Leader to support the NRC’s Clean Energy Innovation Research Centre in Ottawa. The Facility Leader would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The successful candidate will work closely with researchers, facility operations staff, contractors, and vendors to maintain and advance the performance of NRC’s state-of-the-art research infrastructure.
The position plays a key role in ensuring that facilities are operated safely, efficiently and in alignment with project requirements, quality standards, budgets and client expectations.
If you’re a technically skilled, safety-minded professional, we’d like to hear from you.
The key responsibilities of the Facility Leader are the following:
- Manages assigned facilities, laboratories and physical resources to maximize utilization, safety, cost efficiency and reliability.
- Prepares annual budget requirements for facility operations and maintenance, managing assigned budgets, and supporting facility rate reviews and cost recovery.
- Oversees maintenance, calibration, troubleshooting, repair and installation of complex equipment, tools and instrumentation.
- Provides functional supervision and guidance to facility coordinators, including workload planning, scheduling, coaching and follow-up.
- Manages, oversees, or supports capital equipment acquisition and installation projects.
- Develops, reviews, or validates technical instructions, protocols, standard operating procedures and laboratory set-ups.
- Designs, plans, conducts and analyzes complex tests and experiments.
- Interacts with clients, project managers, researchers, engineers, vendors and internal service groups to coordinate work and resolve issues.
- Supports project planning, delivery, quality assurance, lessons learned and continuous improvement.
- Develops tools and procedures in support of implementing NRC’s safety-related programs, such as the hazard prevention program (HPP).
- Oversees or leads the implementation of specific health and safety programs.
- Promotes and adheres to NRC’s established health, safety, and environmental standards
- Participates in hazard identification, risk assessment, and mitigation planning.
- Provides appropriate on-the-job instruction and orientation to staff on HSE programs and procedures.
- Reports safety and environmental concerns and proposes improvements to enhance workplace safety and compliance.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Post-secondary education in a technical, engineering or scientific discipline related to the position from a recognized university.
A combination of a post-secondary degree in another field with significant work experience relevant to the position will be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Significant experience in managing activities in a research institute or industrial research facility or laboratory including scheduling of resources, equipment calibration, operation and maintenance, training and oversight of laboratory users, and purchasing and inventory control, preferably in a chemistry or materials processing related setting.
- Experience in setting up, maintaining, and optimizing research laboratories or facilities.
- Significant and recent experience in implementing environmental, health and safety programs in a laboratory environment.
- Experience working in multi-disciplinary teams and functional supervision of technical staff.
- Experience working with internal and external clients, vendors, suppliers, researchers, engineers, project managers and health and safety representatives.
- Experience coordinating small projects or capital projects, including planning, resourcing, risk management and delivery.
- Experience designing and implementing processes and procedures in a research facility environment including those related to health and safety.
- Experience providing advice and support to management related to facility investments and health and safety.
"Significant" refers to 2 to 6 years of experience and "recent" refers to experience obtained within the last 3 years.
Condition of employment
Reliability Status
For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
Bilingual Imperative CBC/CBC
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Knowledge of facility, laboratory or technical service operations, including equipment scheduling, maintenance, calibration, procurement and inventory management.
- Knowledge of research facility practices, quality assurance, standard operating procedures and good laboratory practices.
- Knowledge of occupational health and safety regulations, procedures and practices required to maintain a safe work environment.
- Ability to troubleshoot complex facility, laboratory and equipment issues and determine practical solutions.
- Ability to prepare technical reports, protocols, and standard operating procedures.
- Ability to use general office software and specialized domain-specific software.
- Ability to interpret technical drawings, instructions, specifications, manuals and scientific or technical literature.
- Ability to set priorities, manage time and adjust resources to meet changing operational and project demands.
- Knowledge of finance and procurement principles, policies and procedures would be considered an asset .
Behavioural competencies
- Technology extension - Communication (Level 3)
- Technology extension - Teamwork (Level 3)
- Technology extension - Conceptual and analytical ability (Level 3)
- Management services - Initiative (Level 3)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile(s): Management Services ; Technology Extension ;
View all competency profiles
Compensation
From $99,281 to $117,859 per annum.
In addition, the incumbent will receive the Bilingualism Bonus of $800 per year.
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Notes
- In 2026, the NRC was chosen as one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, a National Capital Region Top Employer and Forbes Canada’s Best Employer.
- Relocation assistance will be determined in accordance with the NRC's directives.
- Must be able to travel locally, nationally and/or internationally.

The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) is an independent agency of the Government of Canada, dedicated to fostering public trust and confidence in Canada's financial system by rigorously regulating and supervising over 400 federally regulated financial institutions (FRFIs) and 1200 federally regulated pension plans (FRPPs). OSFI has offices located in 4 major cities across Canada: Ottawa, Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver. Safeguarding Canada’s Financial Future: Through diligent regulation and supervision of FRFIs and FRPPs, we ensure that these entities operate soundly and securely. Our proactive approach to risk management and early intervention safeguards the interests of depositors, policyholders, pension plan members, and beneficiaries. We remain committed to fostering public confidence and supporting the competitive and resilient nature of Canada's financial landscape. Our Mandate: Our mandate is to ensure the stability and integrity of Canada's financial system. We achieve this by: Maintaining Financial Soundness: Ensuring that FRFIs and FRPPs remain in sound financial condition. Safeguarding Against Threats: Ensuring that FRFIs protect themselves against threats to their integrity and security, including foreign interference. Proactive Intervention: Acting swiftly when issues arise, requiring FRFIs and FRPPs to implement necessary corrective measures without delay. Risk Management: Continuously monitoring and evaluating risks, promoting sound risk management practices among FRFIs and FRPPs. Our Approach: In fulfilling our mandate, we adopt a balanced approach: For FRFIs: We protect the rights and interests of depositors, policyholders, and financial institution creditors. At the same time, we recognize the need for FRFIs to compete effectively and take reasonable risks. For FRPPs: We safeguard the rights and interests of pension plan members, former members, and entitled beneficiaries. Join Us: Be part of a system that ensures financial stability and security for all Canadians. Learn more about our work and how you can contribute to a stronger Canadian financial future. The Royal Canadian Mint (the Mint) is hiring a Senior Program Manager, Treasury Operations who can thrive in a dynamic and inclusive environment.
Reporting to the Senior Director, Treasury Services the Senior Program Manager is responsible for supporting the development, implementation and ongoing management of the Mint’s Treasury Services capabilities, including the establishment and operation of the precious metals trading desk. The position is responsible for supporting customer pricing and trade execution, executing related market hedges, monitoring market activity and exposures, and contributing to the development of trading processes, systems, controls, and reporting.

- Lead Treasury Services initiatives and projects, coordinating stakeholders and deliverables from pilot through implementation.
- Develop and maintain trading procedures, governance and controls that align with established policies, professional standards and risk frameworks.
- Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders, customers, bullion banks and other financial counterparties.
- Monitor performance and drive continuous improvement, identifying opportunities to enhance profitability, customer service, operational efficiency and controls.
This position offers flexible telework arrangements. The incumbent will work primarily from their home workspace and will be required to travel occasionally to the Ottawa facility, based on operational needs and to participate in activities identified by their manager and other key collaborators.

- Demonstrated experience with customer pricing, trade execution and hedging of market exposures in an institutional or financial-market environment.

title: Senior Security Analyst
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - non-imperative
Senior Security Analyst
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
In addition to the position being staffed, this competition may be used to fill similar opportunities (Regular or Term) that become available at the same job grade. If you’re interested in this type of role, we encourage you to apply.
What you will do Reporting to the Senior Manager, Security Threat Monitoring, Screening and Access Programs, you will be the Bank's senior technical specialist for complex personnel security assessments and risk analysis. You will handle highly sensitive information with discretion and sound judgment, following privacy, confidentiality, information-handling and need-to-know requirements.
You will assess high-risk screening cases, including adverse information, unresolved security concerns, Resolution of Doubt, Reviews for Cause and enhanced screening.
You will provide expert advice to support personnel security decisions, working alongside Screening Analysts and the Screening Manager. You will also support Threat Monitoring and incident response when demand increases.
Specifically, you will:
Lead Complex Personnel Security Assessments
- Assess complex, escalated personnel security cases involving adverse information, elevated risks or unresolved concerns.
- Gather, verify and analyze information from authorized internal and external sources to identify concerns, credibility issues, vulnerabilities and mitigating factors.
- Evaluate risks based on duties, access and organizational exposure, and provide evidence-based recommendations to management.
Conduct Security Interviews
- Plan and conduct fair, objective security screening and Resolution of Doubt interviews tailored to identified risks.
- Verify information, assess the credibility and consistency of responses, and document findings for assessments and recommendations.
Support Resolution of Doubt
- Analyze criminal, financial, association, credibility and behavioural concerns to support Resolution of Doubt.
- Develop assessment and interview plans, and coordinate information gathering with internal and external partners.
- Ensure assessments follow applicable policies, standards, procedural fairness and personnel security principles.
Conduct Advanced Open-Source Intelligence Research and Analysis
- Conduct advanced open-source intelligence (OSINT) research to verify information and identify personnel security concerns and emerging risks.
- Evaluate source credibility, reliability and limitations, and document research methods, findings and conclusions.
- Provide OSINT expertise for personnel security, threat assessments and complex work across teams.
Prepare Findings, Assessments and Recommendations
- Prepare clear, accurate and defensible assessment reports, case summaries and briefings that meet applicable policies and standards.
- Present balanced, evidence-based recommendations to decision-makers on risks, mitigation measures, conditions, monitoring and organizational impacts.
Provide Technical Leadership
- Advise analysts and management as the technical expert on complex personnel security assessments, interviewing and risk analysis.
- Review complex, sensitive or precedent-setting files, identify quality gaps and improve standards, procedures and tools.
- Mentor and coach Screening Analysts to strengthen analytical, interviewing and risk assessment skills.
Support Threat Monitoring and Incident Response
- Support Threat Monitoring during heightened threats, major events, incidents, employee safety concerns or increased demand.
- Use OSINT and internal and external information to assess emerging threats, actors and behaviours affecting the Bank, its employees, operations, assets and reputation.
- Prepare threat assessments, intelligence reports and briefings, and provide rapid analysis, escalation and decision support during incidents and crises.
- Stay current on evolving threats and tactics, and improve monitoring, analytical methods and intelligence sharing.
What You Need to Succeed
You are an experienced security professional with expertise in personnel security screening, assessing adverse information, risk analysis and security interviews.
You use sound judgment to balance security risks, organizational needs, privacy, procedural fairness and risk-management principles when making recommendations.
You demonstrate:
- Advanced knowledge of personnel security screening processes, standards, and practices.
- Advanced knowledge of personnel security risk assessment methodologies.
- Experience supporting Resolution of Doubt activities, enhanced screening reviews, and Reviews for Cause processes.
- Experience conducting security screening interviews and fact-finding interviews.
- Strong analytical and critical-thinking abilities.
- Advanced OSINT research and analytical capabilities.
- Experience preparing assessment reports, security assessments, risk assessments, briefing notes, and recommendations for management.
- Strong written communication, briefing, and presentation skills.
- Exceptional judgment, discretion and attention to detail, with a demonstrated ability to protect highly sensitive personal and security information and share it only on an authorized need-to-know basis.
- Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
- Ability to mentor and provide technical guidance to others.
- Ability to influence decisions through expertise, rigorous analysis and professional credibility, without formal authority.
Nice-to-Have
- Experience conducting complex personnel security assessments.
- Experience supporting Reviews for Cause and other personnel security review processes.
- Experience conducting OSINT activities related to personnel security or threat assessment matters.
- Knowledge of Government of Canada security screening standards and best practices.
- Experience working with law enforcement, intelligence, regulatory, or security partners.
- Experience developing assessment methodologies, procedures, or analytical frameworks.
Education and Experience This position requires a bachelor's degree in Criminology, Security Studies, Intelligence Studies, Psychology, Sociology, Law, Public Administration, Political Science, International Relations, Business Administration or a related discipline and a minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in personnel security screening or assessments, security risk assessment, intelligence analysis, threat assessment, law enforcement, regulatory investigations or related security functions. An equivalent combination of education and experience may also be considered.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.
What you need to know
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Top Secret Relocation assistance may be provided, if required Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.
Hybrid Work Model
The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .
- Salaries are based on qualifications and experience and typically range from $111,051 to $130,649 (job grade 17) The Bank offers an incentive for successfully meeting expectations at 7 to 10% of your base salary. The Bank offers additional performance pay (5%) for those who exceed expectations. Exceptional performers who far exceed expectations may be eligible for higher performance pay. Flexible and comprehensive benefits so you can choose the level of health and dental coverage that meets your needs Extra vacation days (up to five each year) that you can purchase to add to your vacation entitlement Option to join the indexed, defined-benefit pension plan after 24 consecutive months of service
We wish to thank all applicants for their interest and effort in applying for this position. Only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

title: Optical Engineer (#26050)
description:
Language requirements: English essential
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
The Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre (HAA) is seeking an Optical Engineer to lead the conception, development and delivery of advanced optical instrumentation and systems for current and future astronomical observatories. The successful candidate will be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect, and Creativity and will work closely with astronomers, engineers, and technical specialists. The role involves translating scientific and technical requirements into practical engineering solutions, developing optical designs and performance analyses such as tolerancing, stray-light, image quality, throughput, and alignment planning. You will make significant contributions to the design, integration, testing, and verification of complex UV/VIS/NIR optical systems, analyze test results, and recommend design improvements or corrective actions as required. Working within multidisciplinary teams, the Optical Engineer will collaborate closely with mechanical, electrical, software, systems, scientific, and technical specialists to develop instrument concepts, perform technical trade studies, and guide engineering decisions throughout the instrument lifecycle. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- leading or contributing to strategic research and development activities;
- investigating and evaluating emerging optical technologies;
- preparing technical documentation such as optical specifications, interface control documents, test and verification plans, alignment procedures, technical reports, and design review materials;
- supporting procurement activities, vendor interactions, component evaluation, and acceptance testing.
The position offers the opportunity to contribute to facility-class astronomical instrumentation, space-based observatories and strategic research and development initiatives, participate in national and international collaborations, and provide technical guidance and knowledge transfer to colleagues, students, and junior staff where appropriate. We welcome applications from candidates at different career stages who can demonstrate strong technical foundations, a commitment to learning, and the potential to contribute to the development of advanced scientific instrumentation.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Graduation with a Masters or PhD from a recognized post-secondary institution in Optical Engineering, Physics, Engineering Physics, Electrical Engineering, or another field relevant to the position. Graduation with a Masters or PhD from a recognized post-secondary institution in Engineering combined with relevant work experience in astronomy or other sectors such as aerospace, space systems, defense, remote sensing, biomedical imaging, photonics, or other precision optical industries may also be considered. As part of their application package, applicants are required to provide the following:
- Cover Letter
- Resume
- 2-page Executive Summary: The summary must describe a relevant project, completed from design to delivery, and include key information such as project overview, optical design, modelled performance, tolerance summary, delivered performance, and lessons learned. Applicants should clearly identify their own role and contributions, and focus on the most important technical aspects of the project, including driving requirements, design choices, performance metrics, and verification strategies. Confidential or proprietary details may be anonymized.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Extensive* experience in optical engineering, including most of the following areas: optical lens design, modelling, performance analysis, tolerancing, procurement, testing, alignment, integration, verification/validation, and optical metrology.
- Significant** experience leading or making substantial technical contributions to at least one optical engineering project through the full lifecycle, including requirements definition, design, integration, testing, verification, and final delivery or acceptance.
* Extensive: Typically 8–10+ years of deep technical experience. ** Significant: Typically 4–5+ years of progressive technical experience.
The following will be considered as assets:
- Experience developing, integrating, or supporting complex, facility-class scientific instruments, observatory-class astronomical instrumentation, mission-class spaceflight payloads, or large-scale remote sensing systems in a multidisciplinary environment.
- Experience designing or building spectrographs, spectrometers, or other dispersive optical instruments. (IFU/IFS, MOS, echelle, slit or slitless)
- Experience designing, specifying, procuring, testing, and aligning custom optics such as dispersive elements, aspherics and free-forms.
- Experience with one or more of the following specialized technologies: Adaptive optics, fiber-fed instruments, detector systems, calibration systems, cryogenic optical systems, precision opto-mechanical systems, photonics.
- Experience applying systems engineering practices to complex scientific or engineering projects, including development of performance budgets (wavefront error, throughput, image/pupil quality) requirements management, interface control, verification and validation, risk management, or technical reviews.
- Experience providing technical leadership, including conceptualizing new instruments, leading technical work packages, coordinating multidisciplinary teams, mentoring technical personnel, or influencing technical decisions.
Condition of employment
Reliability Status For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Optical Design Knowledge: Depth and breadth of knowledge in optical engineering theory, design, modelling, and analysis. This may include optical system and lens design; optical modelling and optimization; tolerancing; wavefront, diffraction, image quality, polarization, fibre, or stray-light analysis; optical performance budgeting; radiometric or throughput modelling; coating design; detector performance modelling; and thermal and flexural analyses.
- Instrument Development, Integration and Delivery: Ability to contribute to the integration, testing, verification, and delivery of optical systems or scientific instrumentation. This may include optical alignment and integration; the use of optical metrology, alignment, and diagnostic equipment; development of alignment and test procedures; procurement of custom optical components and assemblies; performance characterization and testing; assembly, integration, and test (AIT) planning and execution; troubleshooting and root-cause analysis; acceptance testing; and interpretation of engineering drawings and optical specifications.
- Technical Problem Solving and Innovation: Ability to identify, analyze, and resolve complex technical challenges.
- Software, Modelling, and Analytical Tools: Knowledge of optical design, modelling, simulation, or data-analysis tools to support engineering decisions. (e.g., Zemax, Code V, FRED, MATLAB, Python, or equivalent tools).
- Technical Communication and Collaboration: Ability to communicate technical information and work effectively in multidisciplinary teams. This may include experience preparing and presenting technical documentation such as design reports, specifications, procurement documents and drawings, test plans and procedures, verification and validation reports, engineering analyses, design review materials, or technical recommendations.

About the Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre
We are Canada's gateway to the stars. At the Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre (HAA), we maintain and operate Canada's largest and most powerful observatories and represent the country in some of the world's leading astronomy initiatives. We are astronomy and astrophysics experts, conducting cutting-edge research, operating Canada's national observatories, providing extensive data management and analysis tools through our Canadian Astronomy Data Centre, supporting activities at international observatories and developing advanced astronomical instruments with industrial partners. More…
About DAO
HAA has a rare combination of staff involved in astronomy research, instrumentation design and development, engineering, data science and observatory support. Our facilities are located on two sites: Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory (DRAO) in Penticton, BC, Canada, and the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory (DAO) in Victoria, BC, Canada. HAA is a leading developer of instrumentation for Canada’s current and future ground- and space-based telescopes at radio through ultraviolet wavelengths, including major facilities such as the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), the Canada France Hawaii Telescope (CFHT), the International Gemini Observatory, and Canada’s flagship space telescope: Cosmological Advanced Survey Telescope for Optical and UV Research (CASTOR). Current and future ground- and space-based facilities from the UV to radio are represented in our instrumentation development, which includes radio astronomical instrumentation (receivers, correlators, antennas, etc) and UV/visible/near-IR instrumentation (spectrographs, imagers, adaptive optics, precision mechanics, photonics, detectors, etc). Our instrument development activities also include the development of pathfinder instruments and on-sky demonstrators. HAA is eager to diversify the fields of research represented at our Research Centre. We are committed to ensuring that all staff members promptly receive the accommodation they need to do their job and we understand the importance of work/life balance. More…

Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) helps the Government of Canada serve Canadians. With a strong focus on quality customer service, we provide innovative common services such as real estate and building management, purchasing, banking, pay and pensions, and translation to other government departments, agencies, and boards. By providing these centralized services to departments and agencies, we enable them to focus on what they do best: providing their programs and services to Canadians.
At PSPC, our approach to inclusion is simple: we are committed to achieving a competent and representative workforce that reflects the diversity of the Canadian population we serve, and strive to create a welcoming, respectful, and inclusive environment that enables collaboration and innovation. When you succeed, we all succeed.
Come join our multi-disciplinary team of environmental professionals and contribute to the Government of Canada’s goals towards a cleaner, greener country. Environmental Services and Contaminated Sites (ESCS), Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) - Ontario Region, provides a wide variety of services to Federal Departments including: Environmental Site Assessments , Human Health and Ecological Risk Assessment, Contaminated Site Remediation, Environmental Assessments in accordance with Impact Assessment Act, Ecological Inventories and Management plans, Waste Reduction, Sustainability, Climate Change, Greenhouse Gas/Energy Studies and other environmental initiatives.
