title: Software Developer and CVR Specialist (#26251)
description:
Language requirements: English essential
The role
We are looking for a Software Developer and Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) Specialist to join our Aerospace Research Centre at the Flight Research Laboratory’s (FRL) Flight Recorder Playback Center (FRPC). You would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The FRPC provides flight data recorder (FDR) data recovery and analysis services to the Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF). These services include data and audio recovery and analysis from aircraft accidents and incidents as well as the annual evaluation of flight data recorder systems and cockpit voice recorders (CVR) installed in aircraft across multiple fleets, using a variety of recording systems from different manufacturers.
As a Software Developer and CVR Specialist, you will develop and maintain software tools at NRC and those provided by FDR manufacturers to play back, process and analyze flight data downloaded from FDRs. You will manage the facility’s internal computer network and coordinate with the corporate IT team from NRC as needed. You will also become NRC’s subject-matter expert for CVR systems, including conducting annual CVR audio evaluations for RCAF aircraft.
FDR and CVR data downloads could arrive daily. You will manage the associated workflow and prepare analysis reports within established timeframes.
Your work will involve:
- Developing, maintaining and enhancing FRPC software tools and databases using Qt, C++, Python, Microsoft Access and VBA;
- Maintaining FRPC procedures, equipment documentation, specialized external software and internal IT systems—including legacy and current Windows environments, basic network administration, and data backup and recovery;
- Conducting annual CVR audio evaluations for RCAF aircraft;
- Supporting CVR requirements development and assessment for new RCAF aircraft acquisitions;
- Supporting flight-recorder recovery activities, including crash-damaged recoveries, and collaborating with the FRPC Facility Manager and NRC IT team; and
- Participating in a rotating on-call schedule with other engineers, including occasional work outside regular business hours.
The ideal candidate will be an organized and adaptable problem solver with strong software-development, computer networking, data-analysis and technical-reporting skills. The candidate will be comfortable working with legacy and modern computer systems, specialized flight-recorder software, and audio hardware systems and analysis procedures. The ideal candidate will be an innovative problem solver who enjoys working hands-on with facilities as well as network and computer systems while collaborating with scientists, engineers, and clients to advance flight safety and Canada’s aerospace research capabilities.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
A bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, computer engineering, systems engineering, electronics or another discipline relevant to the position.
A masters’ degree or specialized training in a relevant technical field will be considered an asset.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Recent experience developing and maintaining software applications, tools, scripts using C++, Python, Qt or similar software technologies; and
- Experience in processing, validating, analyzing and reporting on technical, engineering or scientific data, including preparing technical reports, visualizations or briefings for clients.
Assets:
- Basic experience configuring, maintaining and troubleshooting computer systems, operating systems, specialized technical equipment, data storage and backup/recovery systems;
- Experience with audio hardware, audio-recording systems or audio analysis;
- Experience working with flight data recorders or cockpit voice recorders.
Condition of employment
Secret clearance
A thorough security clearance process will be applied.
For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Knowledge of software development and maintenance, including coding, debugging, testing, and documentation of C++, Python and/or Qt for technical applications and data-processing;
- Knowledge of configuring and troubleshooting legacy and current computer systems, various operating systems, storage, backups, and data recovery;
- Knowledge of database concepts, including data structures, queries, data integrity, and routine maintenance of Microsoft Access and VBA for managing, retrieving and reporting of data;
- Knowledge of network hardware, connectivity, shared resources, user access management, and basic network troubleshooting; and
- Basic knowledge of the audio recording process, hardware systems and audio signal fundamentals, including audio quality, gain, headroom, noise and distortion.

The Isthmus of Chignecto, the land bridge between New Brunswick and Nova Scotia, has been a focus of overland travel routes for centuries for the area's Indigenous people and the Europeans who followed. In the heart of Mi'kma'ki, in the Chignecto isthmus, this star-shaped fort, built in 1751, became the scene of three acts of war between France and Great Britain, the deportation of the Acadians and the tearing apart of British North America.
History buffs and culture lovers will enjoy touring the ruins of a star-shaped fort that was vital to the 18th-century struggle between France and Britain over Acadie. Kids can dress up like “gate guards” and patrol the fort’s earthen glacis, casemates and battlegrounds. The site’s wide-open spaces make for wondrous kite flying, bird watching and picnics. About the position
Duties
Assists with field work in ecological monitoring, and with the prevention of human-wildlife conflicts for Parks Canada operations. Assists with the management of data collected as part of ecological monitoring programs. The person selected for the position will work at Kouchibouguac National Park, where they will help ecologists and technicians carry out research on ecology, as well as monitoring the wildlife, vegetation, and environment of the park.
Work environment
Kouchibouguac National Park extends over 238-square-kilometres of Maritime Plain Natural Region along New Brunswick’s scenic Acadian Coast. This mosaic of salt marshes, peat bogs, freshwater systems, Wabanaki-Acadian forest and sandy beaches has long captivated guests, one generation to the next.
Hundreds of species of birds, dozens of mammals as well as amphibians, reptiles, rare plants and a wide variety of sea life inhabit this park, and the landscape welcomes exploration via its network of gentle hiking and cycling trails. Offshore, shifting sand dunes harbour the endangered piping plover and a colony of grey seals swim in the sea. Stargazing takes a unique perspective in this coastal Dark Sky Preserve. Kellys Beach is one of the region’s most popular summertime destinations. And in winter, the snowy side of Kouchibouguac invites soft adventure with cross-country trails and cozy warm-up huts.

description:
Language requirements: English essential
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are looking for a Technical Advisor, Application Development to support our Chief Information Officer Branch (CIOB). The Technical Advisor, Application Development would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
If you love data, then we need you! We have embarked on a multi-year initiative to consolidate multiple Sales, Grants & Contributions, and traditional Case Management applications into one enterprise CRM solution. This solution leverages the Microsoft Platform (D365, Microsoft Portals, MS Power BI) with various third-party add-ons.
We are looking to hire a Technical Advisor that brings an enthusiasm for building Business Intelligence (BI) solutions that are forward thinking with considerations for re-use, maintainability and extensibility. The incumbent is someone to provide expert advice, research, analysis, development and design of BI applications and related strategies.
Key activities:
- Provide specialized advice to internal project teams and work units on technical solutions and standards to adapt and support the design, development, testing, implementation, integration, maintenance and support of BI solutions;
- Advise and guide business clients on technical applications issues, and provides expertise and analysis to facilitate client understanding, involvement and acceptance of the design, development, testing and delivery, installation, integration and maintenance of BI applications;

title: Clinical/Forensic Psychologist
description:

About CSE
The Communications Security Establishment (CSE) is Canada’s agency responsible for foreign signals intelligence, cyber operations and cyber security. Learn more about our mission , and what it means to work in a security and intelligence field .
CSE is committed to fostering a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion. This isn’t just an ideal, it’s crucial to our mission. Find out about our workplace culture , including our diversity and inclusion initiatives.
Become part of our team and you’ll understand why CSE is the most important organization you’ve never heard of (YouTube) .
Job summary
In this role you will perform psychological assessments on potential candidates and current employees. You will be responsible to administer and interpret standardized psychological tests and conduct psychological interviews. Your assessment reports will offer advice and recommendations about the suitability and organizational complementarity of candidates, or about the psychological readiness of employees for a mission.
Salary
To find out more about our salary scale, vacation allowances and benefits (health, dental and pension plans, etc.) visit the Compensation page on our website.
Area of selection
Open to Canadian citizens.
Location
Ottawa, Ontario. CSE has two accessible facilities . Flexible work arrangements, including telework for a portion of the work week, may be possible.
Conditions of employment
An Enhanced Top Secret (ETS) security clearance is a condition of employment that must be met before an offer can be made.
More information about our hiring and security processes can be found on our website.
Essential qualifications
In order to be considered, your cover letter must clearly explain how you meet the following education and experience requirements.
Education
- Hold a master's or doctoral degree in psychology from a recognized university with a specialization in clinical or forensic psychology, and
- Be an active member of the College of Psychologists of Ontario, the Order of Psychologists of Quebec or in your province of residence and be authorized to practice independently, as a psychologist, in the field of forensic or clinical psychology.
Note: The educational program must be recognized in Canada, and you must be able to provide proof of education credentials.
Experience
- Conducting psychological assessments with adults, including experience in assessing personality, emotional and behavioral functioning and psychopathology.
- Administering and interpreting standardized psychological assessment instruments (ie. MMPI-2; MMPI-3 MMPI-RF, PAI, NEO-PI)
- Writing psychological reports and communicating psychological assessment results in a clear, concise and professional manner.
Official language requirements
Bilingual imperative: CCC/CCC
- Bilingual means that knowledge of both official languages (English and French) is required for the position. Imperative means that you must possess the knowledge of both official languages before a job offer can be made.
- The profile (CCC/CCC) represent the proficiency level you must demonstrate in each of the language skills (reading, writing and oral interaction) for the bilingual position. For bilingual positions, second language evaluations will be offered to candidates who don’t have valid language test results issued by the Government of Canada.
Find out more about the language requirements of positions.
Competencies
The following technical, behavioural and leadership competencies will be assessed at a later date. You do not need to include information about them in your application.
Technical competencies
- Knowledge of Clinical Psychology (Psychopathology, Mental Health Issues and Treatment)
- Knowledge of Methods Related to Individual Psychological Assessment of Adults
- Consultation Services, Communication and Education on Psychological Indicators and Behavioural (which may pose a Risk for the Organization)
Behavioural competencies
- Accountability/Autonomy
- Cognitive Thinking Skills
- Interactive Communication
- Working in a Team
Leadership competencies
- Achieving Results
- Collaboration
- Integrity, Respect and Awareness
Assets
Assets are “nice-to-have” expertise and skills we’re interested in.
Please demonstrate on your application if you meet or possess the asset experience listed below.
Asset experience
- Completing psychological assessments that are relevant to personnel selection in a high security environment.
How to apply
You may submit your candidacy online by selecting “Apply” at the top or bottom of this page.
If you cannot apply online or have a disability preventing you from applying online, please inform us by email at careers-carrieres@cse-cst.gc.ca prior to the closing date of this hiring process.
Important information
We ask you to not discuss your application with others (including on social media) besides your partner, or close family members - who should also be reminded about the need to be discreet.
Assessments of candidates are conducted in the official language of their choice.
To address CSE’s current representation gaps, priority may be given to persons who self-declare as belonging to one, or more, designated employment equity groups: women; Indigenous peoples, including First Nations who are status, or registered and non-status, or non-registered, Inuit and Métis; persons with disabilities, including people with a mental health condition and neurodivergent people; and persons from racial or ethnic groups.
Please note the Employment Equity Act , which is under review, uses the terminology Aboriginal peoples and visible minorities.
CSE offers an assessment process that will accommodate any reasonable measures you require to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner. Those measures are available to all candidates during our processes. Information you provide will be addressed confidentially.
All communications with CSE relating to this process, including email messages and telephone conversations, may be used in the assessment of qualifications.
The intent of this process is to fill vacant positions at CSE. The process may also be used to establish a pool of qualified candidates which could be used to staff similar or identical positions with various tenures.
Due to the nature of CSE’s mandate certain roles may expose employees to content that is difficult to process. Mental health is a priority at CSE and if any personnel feel they require assistance to preserve their mental wellbeing, they have access to services, tools and other resources to help them in both their personal and professional lives.
Please note that in an effort to maintain balance between employee development and business needs, candidates who are hired at CSE must remain in their substantive position for a minimum of twelve (12) months subject to operational requirements.
We thank you for your interest in CSE. However, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

Interactions with law enforcement, credit history, personal associations, and other relevant security considerations may also affect a candidate’s eligibility to be granted the required security screening level and may influence the time needed to complete the security screening process.

Company Description
The Library of Parliament is a non-partisan organization that provides a unique and stimulating work environment. We are led by our guiding principles of agility, collaboration, excellence, impartiality, and inclusion. For more information about the Library and what we offer, visit Employment opportunities at the Library of Parliament .
Job Description
Reporting to the Senior Manager, Data Analysis and Visualization, the Data Librarian helps the Library of Parliament deliver research services to parliamentary clients through data analysis, data visualization, geospatial analysis and mapping.
The incumbent’s duties include the following:
- Searches, identifies, evaluates, collects, groups, organizes and updates an extensive array of geospatial data sources, and facilitates access to them.
- Analyzes the information needs of Library staff and parliamentary clients to ensure access to statistical and geospatial data that meet their needs.
- Implements quality control procedures to evaluate the accuracy, completeness and reliability of data requested by Library staff and parliamentary clients.
- Responds verbally or in writing to reference and information requests related to data and statistics.
Qualifications
Education :
- A Master of Library and Information Science (MLIS) OR
- A Master of Information Studies (MIS) degree from an institution accredited by the American Library Association (ALA), or from a recognized accrediting body deemed equivalent by the ALA.
Experience :
- Experience working with large and complex datasets from multiple sources and covering different time periods.
- Experience conducting in-depth searches using print and electronic resources.
- Experience providing reference and information services to clients.
- Experience providing written responses to clients’ requests for information.
Knowledge :
- Knowledge of authoritative Canadian and international sources of statistical and/or geospatial data in various fields related to federal public policy.
- Knowledge of search methods, techniques and tools associated with retrieving and evaluating information.
Competencies :
- Adaptability
- Client Focus
- Embracing Diversity
- Exemplifying Integrity
- Organizational Awareness
- Data Information Retrieval and Analysis
- Quality Focus
- Communication
- Teamwork
- Analytical Thinking
Asset Criteria :
- Experience working with Statistics Canada datasets, including survey and Census of Population data.
- Experience using advanced Microsoft Excel features and functions.
- Experience developing, managing and maintaining large, high-quality databases and datasets.
- Knowledge of geography, cartography, geographic information systems, and related information and data sources.
Conditions of Employment :
- A successful pre-employment security screening.
- A second-language evaluation (Bilingual staffing – imperative): CCC/CCC.
Second language self-assessment test:
To help you decide if you should apply to a bilingual position, an optional self-assessment of your written expression and reading comprehension in your second official language is available for you to take before completing your application.
Try out the self-assessment tests for written expression and reading comprehension.
For more information on language requirements, see the language requirements for candidates .
Additional Information
Please include a cover letter with your application describing how you meet the education and experience requirements of the position. Applications without a cover letter may not be considered . Please combine your cover letter and CV into a single document or upload your cover letter on the second page of the application form.
The Library of Parliament welcomes all candidates to apply and encourages applications from Indigenous persons, racialized persons, 2SLGBTQIA+ persons and persons with disabilities for this position.
We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace by providing a barrier-free staffing process. If you have an accommodation request or require material in an accessible format, please contact us at LOPCareers-CarrieresBDP@parl.gc.ca .
Education and experience requirements will be used to determine which candidates will be asked to participate in the next stage of the selection process.
This selection process may include a second-language evaluation, a written exam, and an interview. The interview will consist of behavioural, situational and knowledge-based questions. Candidates will be required to pass each stage in order to move to the next stage of the selection process.
Qualified candidates from this selection process may be considered for determinate or indeterminate positions at the Library of Parliament that require similar knowledge and/or competencies.
Satisfactory references and proof of education are essential conditions of appointment.
Travel and relocation expenses are the responsibility of the candidates.
Visit About the Library of Parliament of Canada to learn more about us!
To learn more about our staffing process, consult our FAQs.

title: Analyst (Legal Counsel)
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Description de l'entreprise
La Bibliothèque du Parlement est un organisme non partisan qui offre un environnement de travail unique et stimulant. Nous sommes guidés par nos principes directeurs d’agilité, de collaboration, d’excellence, d’impartialité et d’inclusion. Pour en savoir plus sur la Bibliothèque du Parlement et sur ce que nous offrons, consultez la page Possibilités d’emploi à la Bibliothèque du Parlement .
Description du poste
Relevant de l’avocate générale du Comité mixte permanent d’examen de la réglementation, l’analyste (conseiller/conseillère juridique) est responsable de fournir des conseils juridiques au Comité mixte sur les lacunes juridiques et procédurales relevées dans les instruments statutaires émanant du pouvoir exécutif.
La personne titulaire du poste assume les tâches suivantes :
- Comparaître devant le Comité mixte afin de fournir des conseils sur des questions juridiques nouvelles et complexes en droit réglementaire et de répondre aux questions des membres.
- Rédiger des avis juridiques pour le client et appliquer les principes juridiques régissant l’exercice des pouvoirs législatifs délégués, l’interprétation des lois et le droit administratif.
- Rédiger des lettres aux ministères et organismes gouvernementaux sur une question juridique ou sa résolution pour le client.
Qualifications
Éducation :
- un baccalauréat en droit (LL.B.) / Juris Doctor (J.D.) obtenu d'une université reconnue, combiné à une adhésion en règle à un barreau provincial ou territorial.
Expérience :
- expérience récente dans la rédaction d’avis juridiques complexes dans l'un des domaines juridiques de la sphère fédérale;
- expérience récente dans la conduite de recherches et d’analyses juridiques en droit réglementaire, interprétation des lois, droit administratif, droit constitutionnel et droit parlementaire.
- récente fait référence à l’expérience acquise au cours des cinq (5) dernières années.
Connaissances :
- connaissance du rôle et du mandat du Comité mixte permanent d’examen de la réglementation;
- connaissance du processus réglementaire fédéral;
- connaissance du droit administratif et des principes juridiques régissant l’exercice des pouvoirs législatifs délégués;
- connaissance des méthodes, techniques et pratiques juridiques, telles que l’interprétation des lois et la recherche juridique (électronique et manuelle).
Compétences :
- Faculté d’adaptation
- Orientation client
- Modèle d’intégrité
- Souci du détail
- Recherche
- Travail d’équipe
- Réflexion analytique
- Communication
- Conscience de l’organisation
Qualifications constituant un atout :
- expérience dans la formulation de conseils et d’avis juridiques et leur présentation adaptée à divers publics;
- expérience de la prestation de services juridiques dans la fonction publique, en cabinet privé ou en milieu parlementaire.
Conditions d’emploi :
- Vérification de sécurité préalable à l’emploi.
- Évaluation de langue seconde (poste bilingue – dotation impérative) : CBC/CBC.
Test d'autoévaluation en langue seconde: Afin de vous aider à décider si vous devriez postuler pour des emplois bilingues, avant de soumettre votre demande, vous pouvez effectuer un test d'autoévaluation facultatif vous permettant d'évaluer vos aptitudes à la rédaction et à la compréhension de l’écrit dans votre seconde langue officielle. Essayez les tests d’autoévaluation pour la compréhension de l’écrit et l’expression écrite avant de passer les tests officiels.
Pour plus de renseignements sur les exigences linguistiques, voir les exigences linguistiques pour les candidats .
Informations supplémentaires
Veuillez joindre une lettre de motivation à votre candidature qui démontre comment vous rencontrez les exigences relatives aux études et à l’expériences du poste. Les candidatures non accompagnées d'une lettre de motivation pourraient ne pas être prises en considération. Veuillez combiner votre lettre de motivation et votre CV en un seul document ou joindre votre lettre de motivation à la deuxième page du formulaire de candidature.
La Bibliothèque du Parlement invite toutes les personnes à postuler et encourage les Autochtones, les personnes racialisées, les membres de la communauté 2ELGBTQIA+ et les personnes en situation de handicap à présenter leur candidature à ce poste.
Nous nous engageons à créer un milieu de travail inclusif en offrant un processus de dotation sans obstacles. Si vous avez une demande de mesure d’adaptation ou besoin de matériel dans un format accessible, veuillez nous contacter à LOPCareers-CarrieresBDP@parl.gc.ca .
Les exigences relatives aux études et à l’expérience seront prises en compte à la première étape du processus de sélection pour déterminer qui participera à l’étape suivante.
Le processus de sélection peut comprendre une évaluation de langue seconde, un examen d’aptitude écrit et une entrevue. L’entrevue comprendra des questions portant sur les comportements, les situations et les connaissances. Les personnes participant au processus de sélection devront réussir chaque étape avant de pouvoir passer à l’étape suivante.
La candidature des personnes qui se qualifieront dans le cadre du présent processus pourra être examinée dans le but de pourvoir des postes à durée déterminée ou indéterminée exigeant des connaissances ou des compétences comparables à la Bibliothèque du Parlement.
Des références satisfaisantes et une preuve de scolarité sont des conditions essentielles de la nomination à ce poste.
Les frais de déplacement et de réinstallation sont à la charge des personnes participant au processus de sélection.
Visitez À propos de la Bibliothèque du Parlement du Canada pour en savoir plus sur nous !
Pour en savoir plus sur notre processus de recrutement, consultez notre Foire aux questions.

About the position
Duties
As part of the MSc program (project), the incumbent will manage and organize a field small plot trial and a lab in vitro studies. Duties include:
• Organize, manage and monitor field small plot trial
• Organize, manage and monitor in vitro lab trial
• Collect and analyze forage and silage samples related to the project
• Collect and analyze data with proper statistical procedure
• Draft reports and contributes to the preparation of research reports and presentations

Work environment
The Forage and Ruminant Nutrition research team at the Swift Current RDC has a crew of two research scientists, three technicians, a livestock manager and 5 general labourer. The successful candidate will manage a research project that involves small plot trial, silage quality assessment as well as an in vitro lab trial. The candidate will work closely with the research team who will provide all the necessary support and guidance. In implementing the project, the successful candidate is willing:
• to join the university of Saskatchewan to complete all the courses needed for the MSc program while managing the research project at the Swift Current RDC.
• to work with the forage and beef research team to manage the project and coordinate research activities in the field and in the lab
• to work under various environmental and weather conditions. The project involves field small plot trial that requires establishment, maintenance and sample and data collection during the summer and fall seasons. Collected samples are prepared and analyzed in the lab during winter and spring seasons.
• to work with beef cattle as the project requires rumen fluid collection from rumen fistulated animals for the in vitro lab analysis.
• to work in a laboratory environment. The forage and beef program has a fully functional ruminant nutrition laboratory where collected samples will be analyzed. Technicians will facilitate and provide all the necessary help while the candidate implement lab analysis protocols to analyze collected samples.

title: Postdoctoral Fellow, Next-Generation Smart Battery Management System (#26200)
description:
Language requirements: English essential
The program
The NRC’s Postdoctoral Fellowship program offers PDFs access to unique world-class facilities and the opportunity to work alongside multi-disciplinary teams of expert researchers and technicians on projects of critical importance to Canada. PDFs will carry out research on innovative research projects, with opportunities for career development (publications and/or industry interaction).
PDFs will be offered appointments to the staff of the National Research Council on a term basis and will be offered salaries and benefits currently available to Research Officers. Salaries commensurate with experience are taxable and subject to other deductions. As a guide, the current annual PhD recruiting rate is $83,985. In addition PDFs will be allocated a travel fund to support their work.
Project title
Next-Generation Battery Management System for Electrified Transportation and Energy Storage
The role
Battery systems are central to electrified transportation, including electric vehicles, trains, and aircraft. Every battery pack requires a battery management system (BMS), an electronic controller that monitors, protects, and optimizes battery operation. Current BMS technology has critical gaps: existing platforms are closed and restrict research use; temperature sensing is sparse, forcing engineers to rely on unreliable simulation models; and the standard cell-balancing method wastes energy as heat.
This project will develop a next-generation, NRC-built BMS platform integrating three novel capabilities: a flexible, cloud-connected architecture for research use; fiber Bragg grating (FBG) optical sensors embedded in battery packs, providing hundreds of real-time temperature sensing points to support thermal management and fast charging; and an active cell-balancing prototype that redistributes energy between cells rather than dissipating it. The project will produce peer-reviewed publications and patent opportunities, and directly supports Canada's net-zero transportation goals.
As the postdoctoral fellow, you will be the primary researcher on this project, taking each of its three components from early-stage work to working hardware. In your first year, you will be a part of the development of the NRC BMS platform, expanding its hardware and software capability. Across both years, you will build on a completed proof of concept to embed FBG sensor arrays into battery modules and connect them to the platform for real-time thermal mapping. In your second year, you will develop a physical active cell-balancing prototype and benchmark it against conventional passive balancing.
You will work with a high degree of autonomy, supported by a project lead and other team members. You will have hands-on access to NRC’s state-of-the-art battery testing facility and will collaborate with researchers across NRC, including the Aerospace and Construction research centres, as well as external partners. In this role, you will build expertise in embedded sensing, power electronics, and software development, and you will be encouraged to publish in peer-reviewed journals, present at conferences, and pursue patents arising from the work.

For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency

- Experience using programming and data analysis software such as Python, MATLAB, or C/C++.
The following experience criteria would be considered assets:
- Experience designing, building, or testing electronic hardware or battery systems in a laboratory setting.
- Experience working with battery management systems and related functions such as state estimation, cell balancing, or thermal management.
- Experience developing circuit design, simulation, or printed circuit board (PCB).
- Experience developing embedded firmware for microcontrollers.
- Experience using cloud connectivity, IoT systems, and connected devices.

description:

Project title
Learning Driver Attention Strategies in Adverse Weather Using Graph-Based Inverse Reinforcement Learning.
The role
The successful candidate will develop a graph-based inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) framework for analyzing and forecasting eye-gaze scanpaths of human drivers of motor vehicles. Our objective is to infer the underlying reward structures that govern gaze behavior and thereby reveal how attention strategies adapt to changing environmental conditions. By applying spectral graph analysis , we aim to derive quantifiable and interpretable metrics that capture shifts in gaze patterns across different weather scenarios. To extend this analysis toward prediction, we will incorporate deep learning model for forecasting future gaze trajectories and future driving action, yielding a complete pipeline from metric extraction to scanpath prediction. To the best of our knowledge, this will be the first in-depth study of driver eye-gaze behavior under adverse weather, representing a novel contribution to the field.
In addition to the project described above, the successful candidate will be part of a multi-disciplinary team of researchers, and will be expected to participate in other projects to ensure a well-rounded post-doctoral training.

Do you want an environment that will encourage growth and development? Do you want to be part of the development of new and innovative applied research? This PDF project positions Canada at the intersection of two national priorities: space exploration and equitable healthcare access.
The long-term vision of this research is to establish autonomous immune monitoring technologies for space exploration and remote healthcare applications. As a critical step toward this vision, the primary objective of this two-year PDF project is to develop and experimentally validate a laboratory prototype of an autonomous centrifugal microfluidic immune monitoring platform.
The project focuses on prototype development, subsystem integration, and analytical performance evaluation. The aim is to develop a novel, platform-based approach for assessing changes in immune function through semi-quantitative analysis of cytokines released following ex vivo stimulation of whole blood. The project is embedded in a larger collaboration effort involving LMU Hospital (Munich, Germany) with support from both the Canadian and European Space Agency.
Integrated into the MD–Precision Diagnostics Team at NRC Boucherville, where you can leverage established expertise, infrastructure, and ongoing research activities, you will lead the experimental design, optimization, integration, and validation of the incubation cartridge and multiplex immunoassay, including data analysis, interpretation, manuscript preparation, and dissemination of results.

title: Postdoctoral Fellow - Uncertainty Quantification and Calibration for Large Language Models (#26282)
description:
Language requirements: English essential
The program
The NRC’s Postdoctoral Fellowship program offers PDFs access to unique world-class facilities and the opportunity to work alongside multi-disciplinary teams of expert researchers and technicians on projects of critical importance to Canada. PDFs will carry out research on innovative research projects, with opportunities for career development (publications and/or industry interaction).
PDFs will be offered appointments to the staff of the National Research Council on a term basis and will be offered salaries and benefits currently available to Research Officers. Salaries commensurate with experience are taxable and subject to other deductions. As a guide, the current annual PhD recruiting rate is $83,985. In addition PDFs will be allocated a travel fund to support their work.
Project title
Uncertainty Quantification and Calibration for Large Language Models
The role
Are you looking for an opportunity to conduct cutting-edge research with real-life impacts? Do you want to grow in a team environment that provides guidance and autonomy? Do you want ownership over outcomes allowing you to present your work at competitive international venues? Look no further we have a rewarding opportunity for you!
Current human-AI interaction is plagued by over-reliance on AI predictions, an inability to distinguish AI-generated content, and the risks of AI-generated falsehoods and deceptions. Quantifying the uncertainty in AI generations is a pathway to mitigating all of these risks.
Traditionally in AI research, a well-designed certainty measure assigns a probability of correctness to each generated output. Combining AI outputs with these interpretable confidence scores is immensely valuable for informed human-AI interaction. In the new era of generative large language models (LLMs), uncertainty quantification becomes less well-defined due to the open-ended nature of LLM outputs (i.e., it is necessary to simultaneously estimate the uncertainty in what is being said, and how it is being said, while dealing with an infinite output space). However, LLMs are now the backbone of most human-facing AI systems. How to meaningfully capture these uncertainties to provide useful context on LLM generations is an active research question.
Separately, recent work suggests that LLMs represent human-interpretable concepts (e.g., emotions, truthfulness, harmfulness, etc.) at intermediate points in their computation. This opens up a new opportunity to inspect uncertainty in the LLMs’ encoding of these concepts, which would enable new insights and intervention mechanisms. To date, we are not aware of any work that applies certainty calibration methods to intermediate model representations.
This project develops methods for uncertainty quantification that can be applied to both output generations, and intermediate features. Foundational work on this subject is both technically challenging and highly applicable to a wide range of open problems. The anticipated research outcomes are appropriate for publication in top-tier international venues for Computational Linguistics and Machine Learning research, such as ACL* conferences, ICLR, or ICML.
The Research Problem
Large language models produce text by iteratively generating a probability distribution over possible next-word choices, then sampling from that distribution. The problem of uncertainty quantification aims to consolidate that probability distribution into a few meaningful and interpretable certainty metrics. Certainty metrics can answer questions about reproducibility (i.e., if asked the same thing again, how likely is the LLM to respond in the same way?), or embedded knowledge (i.e., if asked a factual query, how certain is the LLM about its prediction?). Such measures can help contextualize LLM outputs for users or developers, and are a critical ingredient for trustworthy AI systems.
The proposed research agenda develops new methods for uncertainty quantification that can apply to features, determines whether such signals can be used to improve uncertainty metrics for text generation, and enables a host of impactful research applications:

description:

Project title
Engineering resilient synthetic microbial consortia for high efficiency ethanol production from syngas.
The role
The NRC is currently working on syngas fermentation for ethanol production, to serve as a replacement for fossil fuels, thus strengthening low-carbon fuel value chains in Canada.
The objective of this project is to develop synthetic microbial consortia with complementary metabolic functions and capable of converting syngas into ethanol with higher efficiency and stability than conventional monoculture systems. The research will comprise three research components:
- Isolate and adapt microbial strains capable of thriving in syngas environments using enrichment and adaptive laboratory evolution;
- Design synthetic microbial consortia composed of microorganisms with complementary metabolic functions;
- Evaluate the performance of these consortia in laboratory-scale bioreactors.
The outcomes of this work will advance the emerging field of microbial community engineering and support the development of scalable technologies for sustainable fuel production and carbon circularity.
Within a multidisciplinary team, the successful candidate will lead the design, construction, and experimental evaluation of synthetic microbial consortia.

description:

The program

Project title
Engineered Recycled Glass as a Supplementary Cementitious Material for Low Carbon, High Performance Concrete ─ Stabilizing the Supply Chain in Canada
The role
Concrete, the most widely used construction material worldwide, is essential for resilient infrastructure but also generates significant greenhouse gas emissions due to cement production. A key strategy for reducing these emissions is lowering the clinker content of cement through supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs). However, the traditional SCM supply chain is shrinking as coal power generation is phased out and steel production technologies evolve, creating an emerging materials challenge for low‑carbon concrete in Canada. This project will address the challenge by investigating ground recycled glass (GRG) as a scalable, sustainable alternative SCM supporting both decarbonization and circular economy objectives.
The PDF will play a central role in designing and executing the experimental research program. Responsibilities will include investigating hydration kinetics and pozzolanic reactivity in cementitious systems incorporating GRG, evaluating the fresh and hardened performance of concrete mixtures, and conducting life cycle and techno-economic assessments.
Education
Ph.D. in Civil Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Cement Chemistry, or a closely related discipline.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Significant experience in cementitious materials research, including cement chemistry, hydration mechanisms, supplementary cementitious materials, concrete performance evaluation, and/or low-carbon concrete technologies.
- Experience in the full spectrum of research activities, including identifying research needs, developing research proposals, planning and managing projects, conducting laboratory investigations, analyzing and interpreting data, and disseminating results through technical reports, presentations, and peer-reviewed publications.
- Experience in the design, execution, and interpretation of laboratory experiments related to cementitious materials and concrete, including analytical characterization techniques, performance testing, durability assessment, and modelling approaches.
- Experience in evaluating concrete durability and long-term performance, including investigation of deterioration mechanisms, service-life assessment methodologies, and performance-based testing approaches.
- Experience in experimental design and statistical analysis, including data collection, quality assurance and quality control, data interpretation, and development of evidence-based recommendations.
- Experience working effectively within multidisciplinary research teams.

description:

About the position
Duties
As an Audit Professional in IT audit, you will work with team members from diverse backgrounds auditing various government entities and systems. Our team is unique in that we work on many of the OAG’s audits while collaborating and advising with OAG staff across Canada.
As IT audit specialists supporting audits at the OAG, we provide advice and assistance in assessing IT risks and leading various IT audits. Mainly, we perform IT general control (ITGC) audits and perform IT risk assessments as they relate to financial audit.
If you enjoy variety and working on diverse, interesting, and challenging projects, and you are resourceful, innovative, and enthusiastic about technology, you would be a great fit for our team!
Your duties will include, but will not be limited to:
-Participating and assisting in ITGC audits, including planning and executing audit procedures, reviewing and analyzing evidence, and documenting processes and procedures;
-Assessing the design, implementation, and operating effectiveness of ITGCs;
-Working with audit team members and audit entities in identifying, analyzing, and documenting IT control risks;
-Establishing and maintaining effective relationships with audit team members and audit entities;
-Developing and communicating clear recommendations that address identified key risks.
Work environment
At the Office of the Auditor General of Canada (OAG), we serve Canadians with the intention of supporting their trust in our public institutions and continued excellence of our public service, one audit at a time.
The OAG employs over 750 people at its head office in Ottawa and regional offices in Vancouver, Edmonton, Montréal, and Halifax. These dedicated employees are brought together to transform Canada’s future and to serve Canada through leadership and partnerships. Specifically, we conduct independent audits and studies that provide objective information, advice, and assurance to Parliament, territorial legislatures, boards of Crown corporations, government, and Canadians.
Intent of the process
This process may be used to establish a pool of qualified candidates to staff similar or identical positions with various security requirements, language requirements, and tenures (indeterminate, term, deployment, acting and assignment).
Important messages
When you apply to this selection process, you are not applying for a specific job, but to an inventory for future vacancies. As positions become available, applicants who meet the qualifications may be contacted for further assessment.
Preference will be given to veterans first, followed by Canadian citizens and permanent residents, with the exception of jobs located in Nunavut or Yukon. Each year, the judges of the Supreme Court of Canada (the Court) select up to 3 law clerks per judge to support them in their work. Law clerks play a vital role by conducting in depth legal research, preparing memoranda of law and assisting with a wide range of tasks essential to the Court’s decision making process.
Clerking at the Court is a unique, career shaping experience . It offers unmatched exposure to complex and significant legal issues, direct mentorship from Canada’s most respected jurists and the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to the development of Canadian jurisprudence. If you strive for excellence, enjoy intellectually rigorous work and are motivated to have real impact at a pivotal stage of your legal career, this role may be the perfect fit.
Intent of the process
The intent of this selection process is to hire up to 27 law clerks to support the Court’s 9 judges.
Who can apply
Persons residing in Canada, and Canadian citizens and Permanent residents abroad.
Preference will be given to veterans first, followed by Canadian citizens and permanent residents.
Learn more about preference to veterans .

Note 2 : Not all law societies recognize law clerk experience toward articling requirements. You are responsible for verifying eligibility with the appropriate law society. - Willingness and ability to work extended hours, including outside core hours and overtime on short notice.
Equity, diversity and inclusion – Self-declaration
The Public Service of Canada is committed to building a skilled and diverse workforce reflective of the Canadians we serve. The Court encourages applicants to self-declare if they belong to any of the designated groups under the Employment Equity Act, S.C. 1995, c. 44 . Applicants may do so in the Application Form.
Equity, diversity and inclusion – Our commitment
The Court is committed to having inclusive, barrier-free selection processes and work environments. If you are contacted about a job opportunity or interview, you should advise the Court in a timely manner of any accommodation measures you require in order to participate fairly and equitably. Please send all accommodation requests to the Law Clerk Program by email: lcp-paj@scc-csc .ca. Information received about accommodation measures will be treated confidentially.
How to apply
Applications for the 2028-2029 Law Clerk Program must be submitted online and received no later than January 7, 2027, at 11:59 pm (Pacific Time) . Your application will be considered complete only once all required materials have been received by the Court.
- 2028‐2029 Law Clerk Program Application
- 2028-2029 Law Clerk Program Reference
Required application materials
- Completed PDF Application Form You must download, save and open the Application Form using a PDF reader. Court communications will be conducted by email and telephone. In your Application Form, you must provide a daytime telephone number where you can be reached or where a message can be left.
- Cover letter Your cover letter must: Be addressed to the Honourable Justices. Explain why you would be an excellent candidate for a law clerk position at the Court by providing, among other things, specific examples that demonstrate: Your experience researching and analyzing Canadian legal issues; and How you meet the competencies stated above. In your Application Form, identify any experience or activities you expect to undertake between the date of your application and the start of a potential clerkship with the Court. If you submit your cover letter in both official languages, you must include both versions in a single document.
- Curriculum vitae If you submit your curriculum vitae in both official languages, you must include both versions in a single document.
- Official law school transcript Official transcripts must be sent directly by the university: By email : lcp-paj@scc-csc.ca By mail : Law Clerk Program Supreme Court of Canada 344 Wellington Street Ottawa, ON K1A 0J1 Note : Secure digital transcripts issued directly by Electronic Transcript Services (secure online platforms that enable law schools to issue official academic documents) are accepted and should be submitted by email to lcp-paj@scc-csc.ca .
- Writing samples You must submit 2 writing samples. Requirements: Each sample must be between 5 and 10 pages in length. Your samples must be relevant to the work of the Court. Your samples must be written solely by you. All pages must be numbered and include your name. New this year , you must provide a summary of a maximum of 80 words for each writing sample in the Application Form, in the same language as the sample. If you are proficient in both official languages, you must submit separate English and French writing samples. Factums prepared for court proceedings or moot court competitions will not be accepted.
- Letters of reference You must provide 4 letters of reference. Requirements: Your letters of reference may be submitted with the application or sent directly by your referees through the 2028-2029 Law Clerk Program Reference online form. One of your 4 letters may be from the Dean of the faculty where you obtained your law degree. A Dean’s letter is optional. Collectively, your letters must provide specific examples demonstrating how you meet the competencies stated above. Your referees should address the competencies they have directly observed in your work, studies or activities. Your letters of reference must be addressed to the Honourable Justices and signed by your referees. Wherever possible, your letters of reference should be printed on official institutional letterhead.
Naming convention
New this year , to ensure the proper processing of applications, all submitted documents, including the completed Application Form, cover letter, curriculum vitae, transcripts, writing samples and letters of reference, must follow the naming convention set out in the table below. Adhering to this convention helps prevent technical issues and allows our systems to accurately identify, sort and process your application materials throughout the selection process.
Requirements:
- Start each file name with the document number (01, 02, 03, etc.) specified in the naming convention below.
- Follow the number with your LAST NAME in uppercase letters, then your first name.
- Do not use commas in file names.
- Use the exact document title provided in the naming convention. If you wish to add details to better identify a document, place the additional information in parentheses at the end of the file name.
- Use only the short hyphen (-) to separate elements of the file name, rather than the longer dash (–) that may be automatically inserted by AI tools or certain software programs.
- When requesting letters of reference, provide your referees with the required document title and ask them to use it when naming their file.
Documents Naming convention For example, if Alex Smith applies, the documents are named as follows:
Application Form 01 LASTNAME FirstName - Application Form 01 SMITH Alex - Application Form
Cover letter 02 LASTNAME FirstName - Cover Letter 02 SMITH Alex - Cover Letter
Curriculum vitae 03 LASTNAME FirstName - CV 03 SMITH Alex - CV
Signed letters of reference 04 LASTNAME FirstName - Reference - Referee’s last name 04 SMITH Alex - Reference – Johnston (Judge)
Copies of transcripts 05 LASTNAME FirstName - Transcript 2 – non official; Transcript 3; etc., if there is more than one transcript. Do not use Transcript 1, as it is reserved for the official law school transcript. Transcript 2 is used for the non-official law school transcripts. 05 SMITH Alex - Transcript 2 – non official (Ottawa University) 05 SMITH Alex - Transcript 3 (Toronto University) 05 SMITH Alex - Transcript 4 (Calgary University)
Writing samples 06 LASTNAME FirstName - Writing Sample 1 06 LASTNAME FirstName - Writing Sample 2 06 SMITH Alex - Writing Sample 1 (Powers of administrative tribunals) 06 SMITH Alex - Writing Sample 2 (1459 QCC)
You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete and that all materials, including the 4 letters of reference, have been received by January 7, 2027 . Incomplete applications will not be considered.
We thank all applicants for their interest in the Program. Only applicants selected for an interview will be contacted. Interviews will be conducted by the judges of the Court via MS Teams during the week of February 22, 2027 , and all hiring will be finalized by March 12, 2027 .
FAQ and contact information
For more information about the Law Clerk Program and the clerkship application process, please consult the Frequently asked questions .
For any other questions, contact the Law Clerk Program: lcp-paj@scc-csc.ca .

title: Bilingual Senior Manager, Data and Information Governance
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
About the role
Join the Enterprise Data and Analytics team, in the Bilingual Senior Manager, Data and Information Governance position, and play a key role in advancing how CMHC manages data as a strategic enterprise asset.
In this role, you will lead the operationalization of enterprise data management capabilities and services across the organization, including data quality, metadata, lineage, reference and master data, data domains, observability and lifecycle controls. Through this work, you will strengthen the quality, consistency and accessibility of CMHC’s data and help ensure it is trusted, discoverable and fit for purpose, enabling reliable reporting and analytics, strong operational performance, regulatory compliance and informed decision-making.
What you’ll do:
- Lead and manage the enterprise Data Management function, including its priorities, service commitments, performance targets, resources and delivery plans.
- Operationalize and continuously improve enterprise capabilities for data quality, metadata, lineage, observability, lifecycle management, data domains, reference data and master data.
- Establish scalable standards, processes and controls to improve the consistency, accessibility, reliability and responsible management of data throughout its lifecycle.
- Oversee enterprise data quality practices, including monitoring, controls, issue management, remediation oversight and continuous improvement for critical data assets and priority domains.
- Advance metadata, business definitions, lineage and domain management to improve data discoverability, understanding, traceability and confidence in reporting and analytics.
- Lead master and reference data services to support consistent enterprise definitions, reduce fragmentation and improve integration and operational efficiency.
- Own and evolve enterprise data management tools and services, including the business ownership and adoption of platforms such as Informatica.
- Collaborate with business, IT, architecture, governance, privacy, security and risk partners; define KPIs, KRIs and service measures; and lead a high-performing team that delivers measurable enterprise value.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in a relevant field such as information management, computer science, business administration, engineering, data management or analytics. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
- A minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in data management, data governance, data quality, metadata management, master/reference data management or a related discipline, including at least 5 years in a leadership role.
- Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, data modelling, data domains, master/reference data, observability and the operationalization of data management services in complex organizations.
- Experience with enterprise data management platforms and tools such as Collibra, Informatica or equivalent technologies.
- Experience working in a regulated environment with strong expectations for data controls, compliance, audit support and risk management.
- The ability to establish performance measures and use KPIs, KRIs and service metrics to guide priorities, decisions and continuous improvement.
- Strong leadership, stakeholder-management and executive-communication skills, with the ability to influence adoption across business, technology and governance communities in both official languages (French and English).
It would be great if you also had:
- A master’s degree in data management, analytics, information systems, business administration or a related discipline.
- An industry-recognized certification such as DAMA Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP), DCAM, CIPP/C or a related credential.
- Experience leading enterprise data management in financial services, a Crown corporation or another regulated, public-interest environment.
- Knowledge of mortgage loan insurance, affordable housing programs, real estate or finance.

title: Strategic Cryptologic Researcher
description:
Language requirements: Various language requirements and/or profiles

About CSE
The Communications Security Establishment (CSE) is Canada’s agency responsible for foreign signals intelligence, cyber operations and cyber security. Learn more about our mission .

Job summary
The Tutte Institute for Mathematics and Computing (TIMC) is a government research institute housed within CSE. TIMC ’s mission is to conduct strategic research that has an impact on the most important scientific challenges faced by the Canadian security and intelligence community and its international partners. TIMC delivers on this mission through a research program in foundational mathematics and computer science, with concentrations in cryptology and machine learning research.
TIMC is seeking highly qualified researchers to contribute to the Mathematical Foundations of Cryptography research area
Strategic Researchers at TIMC work on a variety of complex challenges and they draw on a variety of tools including deep mathematical theory and cutting-edge computational resources. Success in this role requires adaptability, creativity, and a passion for advancing knowledge.
Key Responsibilities:
- Conduct high-quality research toward TIMC research focus topics.
- Identify research problems and projects in alignment with CSE’s research strategy.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues at TIMC, across CSE, and with external partners.
- Disseminate research results through technical reports, presentations, peer-reviewed publications, and software contributions.
- Maintain situational awareness in research developments and provide advice and guidance to clients and decision-makers.
Salary
To find out more about our salary scale, vacation allowances and benefits (health, dental and pension plans, etc.), visit the Compensation page on our website.
Area of selection
Open to Canadian citizens.
Location
The majority of our jobs are in Ottawa, Ontario. CSE has two accessible facilities . Flexible work arrangements, including telework for a portion of the work week, may be possible.
Conditions of employment
A valid Enhanced Top Secret (ETS) security clearance is a condition of employment that must be met before an offer can be made.
More information about our hiring process and security page can be found on our website.
Essential qualifications
In order to be considered, your cover letter must clearly explain how you meet the following education and experience requirements.
Education
You must have either one of the following:
- A MSc in mathematics, statistics, computer science or a related field, with at least eight (8) years of post-MSc research experience.
- A PhD in mathematics, statistics, computer science or a relevant field, with at least three (3) years of post-PhD research experience.
Note: The educational program must be recognized in Canada, and you must be able to provide proof of education credentials.
Experience
- Conducting original research with tangible impact in cryptography, quantum information theory, combinatorics, algebra, number theory or a relevant scientific field demonstrated by sustained contributions of publication, presentation and/or code-release. Examples include papers in peer-reviewed journals and proceedings, presentations at top conferences, and widely recognized contributions to software projects.
- Designing, developing, implementing, and/or evaluating novel cryptanalytic methods, computational algorithms, or practical cryptologic applications.
- Leading research teams and/or supervising junior researchers, post-docs or graduate students.
- Establishing and executing research programs, demonstrated, for example, by successful grant applications, contributing to strategic planning, and achieving key project milestones.
Official language requirements
Various language profiles, including English Essential and Bilingual Imperative (CBC/CBC)
- English essential means that the position is unilingual English.
- Bilingual means that knowledge of both official languages (English and French) is required for the position.
- CBC/CBC represent the proficiency level you must demonstrate in each of the language skills (reading, writing and oral interaction) for the bilingual position. For bilingual positions, second language evaluations will be offered to candidates who don’t have valid language test results issued by the Government of Canada.
Find out more about the language requirements of positions.
Competencies
The following technical, behavioural and leadership competencies will be assessed at a later date. You do not need to include information about them in your application.
Technical competencies
- Knowledge and Application of a Field of Mathematics, Computer Science, Physics or Engineering
- Cryptography and Cryptanalysis
- Application Development
- Problem Formulation and Response
Behavioural competencies
- Accountability/Autonomy
- Interactive Communication
- Working in a Team
Leadership competencies
- Achieving Results
- Change and Innovation
- Collaboration
Assets
Assets are “nice-to-have” expertise and skills we’re interested in.
Please demonstrate on your application if you meet or possess the asset experience listed below.
Asset competenciesh3>
The following asset technical, behavioural and leadership competencies will be assessed at a later date. You do not need to include information about them in your application.
Asset technical competencies
Machine Learning
Operational requirements
Overtime and standby duty may be required.
How to apply
You may submit your candidacy online by selecting “Apply” at the bottom of this page.
Note: Be prepared to provide two (2) letters of reference regarding your research experience upon request.
If you cannot apply online or have a disability preventing you from applying online, please inform us by email at careers-carrieres@cse-cst.gc.ca Important information
We ask you to not discuss your application with others (including on social media) besides your partner, or close family members - who should also be reminded about the need to be discreet.
Assessments of candidates are conducted in the official language of their choice.
We are committed to a diverse and representative workforce and an open and inclusive work environment; as such we encourage candidates to self-declare as members of the following designated employment equity groups : women; Indigenous peoples, including First Nations who are status, or registered and non-status, or non-registered, Inuit and Métis; persons with disabilities, including people with a mental health condition and neurodivergent people; and persons from racial or ethnic groups.
Please note the Employment Equity Act , which is under review, uses the terminology Aboriginal peoples and visible minorities.
CSE offers an assessment process that will accommodate any reasonable measures you require to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner. Those measures are available to all candidates during our processes. Information you provide will be addressed confidentially.
The level of competence demonstrated in the various assessments will be used to determine your qualifications for the UNMA 09, UNMA 10 or UNMA 11 level.
All communications with CSE relating to this process, including email messages and telephone conversations, may be used in the assessment of qualifications.
The intent of this process is to fill vacant positions at CSE. The process may also be used to establish a pool of qualified candidates which could be used to staff similar or identical positions with various tenures.
Due to the nature of CSE’s mandate certain roles may expose employees to content that is difficult to process. Mental health is a priority at CSE and if any personnel feel they require assistance to preserve their mental wellbeing, they have access to services, tools and other resources to help them in both their personal and professional lives.
Please note that in an effort to maintain balance between employee development and business needs, candidates who are hired at CSE must remain in their substantive position for a minimum of twelve (12) months subject to operational requirements.
We thank you for your interest in CSE. However, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

About the position
Duties

• Assist in the design and development of training programs, course syllabuses, methodologies, and schedules for training astronauts, mission controllers, instructors, and peers.
• Deliver training to mission controllers, instructors, and ground support personnel from CSA, NASA, and other international partners using multi-media facilities and/or simulations.

Work environment
Depending on the nature of the work required by the position and operational needs, hybrid and flexible work arrangements—such as a combination of on-site work and telework, as well as compressed work schedules—may be offered.
In line with current direction from the Treasury Board Secretariat, the Canadian Space Agency is currently implementing a hybrid work model. Employees are required to work on-site at least four days per week, or the equivalent of 80% of their regular schedule, in accordance with the agreement to be discussed with their supervisor. Depending on the role, some positions could require full-time on-site presence. These arrangements are subject to change based on evolving government direction and organizational needs. Employees are required to comply with the Direction on prescribed presence in the workplace, as well as any subsequent updates.
Intent of the process
The immediate intent is to staff two (2) positions for an indeterminate period. A pool of qualified candidates will be created in order to staff similar positions of varying durations (indeterminate, term, acting, secondment, or assignment), with different language profiles and security levels.

2

They are required to act impartially and to avoid any real, apparent, or potential conflicts of interest, particularly in relation to employment or external activities, gifts, preferential treatment, or post-employment situations.

title: Director, Prevention & Field Operations (#26126)
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
Help bring research to life and drive your career forward with the National Research Council of Canada (NRC), Canada's largest research and technology organization.
We are looking for a dynamic and collaborative Director to provide leadership to the Prevention and Field Operations Directorate of the Health, Safety and Environment Branch and to the leaders within the organization. The Director would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Branch develops and delivers initiatives for the purpose of strengthening occupational health and safety (OHS) and environmental management throughout NRC. HSE branch develops and implements policies for the purpose of protecting people and the environment from the risks associated with NRC’s operations and to accurately identify and reduce associated liability while providing NRC with OHS and environmental services that include guidance and support to our operations for the purpose of complying with applicable policies and legislative requirements.
The successful candidate provides strategic and operational leadership in the management of Occupational Safety & Health and Environmental Stewardship activities ensuring that these activities are aligned with NRC’s strategic goals and impacts. The individual oversees the delivery of high quality services through the implementation of policy instruments, and ensures that systems are in place to maintain compliance, as well as reports on these as required. In addition, they will oversee a group of PFO Managers across the Council from their homebase in Ottawa.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
University degree in engineering, business, science, industrial hygiene or in a related field from a recognized university or an equivalent combination of education and recent practical experience in a similar environment may be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Recent and relevant experience in leading and managing, human and financial resources.
- Recent and relevant experience in establishing and maintaining strong collaborative working relationships with internal or external partners and stakeholders.
- Recent and relevant experience in providing direction and guidance on occupational health & safety and/or environmental stewardship within the public sectors including. Understanding private sector requirement (municipal, provincial) would be an asset.
- Recent and significant experience in providing strategic and operational direction to staff and in managing comprehensive health, safety and environmental programs, services and products.
- Experience developing and implementing policies, procedures and supporting systems for occupational health and safety as well as environmental management.
- Experience providing advice and briefings to executives, management boards and external stakeholders.
Assets
- Strong leadership skills in the management of people (managers) to align to vision and goals.
Condition of employment
Secret clearance
A thorough security clearance process will be applied.
For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.
Language requirements

Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests

Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Ability to develop strategies and options to mitigate risks related to health, safety and environment.
- Proven ability to influence others and get results.
- Ability to seek improvements, make changes and incorporate ideas into practical business applications.
- Recent and comprehensive knowledge of government policies, legislation and regulation, emerging trends and best practices in health, safety and environmental stewardship.
- Ability to lead, build and motivate individuals and teams to meet or exceed performance expectations, particularly through significant organizational change.
- Ability to build internal alliances with clients to understand and meet their needs and to set direction based on these needs.
- Ability to manage effectively in a complex and continuously changing business and technology environment.

- Drive for Results and Efficiency (Level 3)
- Leverage Collaborative Relationships (Level 3)
- Financial Management (Level 2)
